दक्ष: Dakṣa m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5 99. 12, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
दधिमुख: Dadhimukha1 m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 12, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 8, 2.
Dadhimukha2 m.: A monkey-chief. Lustrous (श्रीमान्); old in age, yet strong (हरिवृद्धो ऽपि वीर्यवान्); he came to Rāma with a large army of fierce monkeys 3. 267. 7.
दक्षकन्या: Dakṣakanyā f. (sg. and pl.): Daughter(s) of Dakṣa. Thirteen in number: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kālā, Anāyus, Siṃhikā, Muni, Krodhā, Prāvā, Ariṣṭā, Vinatā, Kapilā, Kadrū 1. 59. 11-13.
दाक्षायणी: Dākṣāyaṇī1 f.: Daughter of Dakṣa. Vinatā so called 1. 27. 24.
Dākṣāyaṇī2 f.: Mother of Rājadharman (Nādījaṅgha), the king of cranes, wife of Kaśyapa 12. 164. 2.
Dākṣāyaṇī3 f.: Divine (देवी); Surabhi so called 12. 167. 3. [See Surabhi]
दाक्षेयी: Dākṣeyī f.: A mythical female bird. Parrots, her progeny 13. 5. 12 (identical with Śukī ? 1. 60. 57).
दारुण: Dāruṇa m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 9, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahmihood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.

Dāruṇa m. (pl.): Name of a people (?) characterized as म्लेच्छ। Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern म्लेच्छ people of the Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … । यवनाश् च सकाम्बोजा दारुणा म्लेच्छजातयः) 6. 10. 63-65; (Dāruṇa, name of a people, or an adjective ‘rough’ describing the म्लेच्छ tribes ?).
दिलीप: Dilīpa m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 15, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
दिवाकर: Divākara m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 14, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
दिशाचक्षुस्: Diśācakṣus m.: A mythical bird living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 10, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
दीर्घदर्शिन्: Dīrghadarśin adj.: ‘One who has fore-thought’. One of the three fishes of the Śakula type is so characterized (the other two being प्राप्तकालज्ञ and दीर्घसूत्र) 12. 135. 3, 2. [See Śakula]
दीर्घसूत्र: Dīrghasūtra adj.: ‘One who procrasti-nates’. One of the three fishes of the Śakula type is so characterized (the other two being प्राप्-तकालज्ञ and दीर्घदर्शिन्) 12. 135. 3, 2. [See Śakula]
दुर्मुख: Durmukha m.: A mythical serpent. Foremost among the serpents (नाग-श्रेष्ट्ःअ); one of those who received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 15, 12.
दैत्यद्वीप: Daityadvīpa m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 11, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
द्रङ्ग: Draṅga m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Takṣaka, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 8, 7, 1.
द्रोण: Droṇa m.: A शार्ङ्गक bird. A. Birth: Fourth son of the sage Mandapāla (turned a शार्ङ्गक bird) and शार्ङ्गिका Jaritā 1. 221. 9; 1. 220. 16, 17; abandoned by the father when he and his brothers were still in the eggs (1. 220. 17), but not abandoned by their mother 1. 220. 19. B. Learning and Status: Mandapāla ex-pected his son Droṇa to become an excellent knower of ब्रह्मन् (ब्रह्मविद् उत्तमः) 1. 221. 9; 1. 225. 3; he became a seer (ऋषि) 1. 220, 19; Agni knew him as such and recognized what Droṇa said in praise of him as ब्रह्मन् 1. 223. 21; 1. 225. 3; Agni addressed him as विभु and ब्रह्मन् 1. 223. 23. C. Khāṇḍava fire: Manda-pāla had already secured from god Agni assurance regarding safety of his children; this was not known to them 1. 220. 21, 31, 32; when the forest was on fire Droṇa and his brothers were abandoned by their mother when they did not act on her advice and enter a hole to save themselves from fire 1. 223 10, 16; Droṇa noticed the advancing fire 1. 223. 5; all the शार्ङ्गक brothers started praising Agni; when his turn came Droṇa praised god Fire and requested him to move away and not touch them as he would not touch the houses in the ocean (? सागरस्य गृहान् इव) 1. 223. 16-19 (Nīla. नदीप्रवाहान् इव अनभि-भाव्यान् स्वाभिभावकांश् च on 1. 232. 19 Bom. Ed.); Agni informed Droṇa that Mandapāla had already interceded on their behalf and further that he was highly pleased with Droṇa's praise; Agni asked Droṇa what he could do for all of them; Droṇa requested him to finish the cats and their relatives who posed a constant threat to their existence 1. 223. 22-24; when the fire subsided, Jaritā returned to her sons and was happy to see them safe 1. 224. 17-19; Mandapāla, too, remembered his sons and returned to them 1. 224. 6, 14, 20; Droṇa and his brothers neither greeted him nor answered his questions 1. 224. 20-22; but in the end all were reconciled 1. 224. 32; 1. 225. 1-4.

Droṇa m.: Name of a mountain. One of the three mountains used by Indra for piling up the fire-altars of the sacrifices of the ancestors of Sulabhā (द्रोणश् च शतशृङ्गश् च वक्रद्वारश् च पर्वतः । मम सत्रेषु पूर्वेषां चिता मघवता सह ॥ ) 12. 308. 183.
द्विविद: Dvivida m.: A monkey-chief. One of the four councillors of Sugrīva 3. 264. 23; according to Tārā, wife of Vālin, they were all noble-minded (महात्मन्), intelligent (बुद्धिमन्त्), and very strong (महाबल) 3. 264. 24; one of the guardians of the army of monkeys of Rāma when it marched towards the southern ocean 3. 267. 19; he, with other monkey-chiefs, kept watch over the bodies of Rāma and Lak-ṣmaṇa lying on the ground bound by the arrows of Indrajit 3. 273. 4; he, with others, applied water, sent by Kubera, to eyes so that they could see beings which had made them-selves invisible 3. 273. 10-13; (in all the above references Dvivida is mentioned in the company of Mainda); Vidura informed Duryodhana that the monkey-chief (वानरेन्द्र) Dvivida hurled a shower of stones on Kṛṣṇa at the gate of Saubha and tried to arrest him with valiant efforts, but did not succeed 5. 128. 41-42.
द्वीपक: Dvīpaka m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 11, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
दण्ड: Daṇḍa m.: A missile associated with Yama, Antaka, Mṛtyu, Kāla, Brahman and Rudra. A. Creation: Indra got heavy Daṇḍas made (कारयाम् आस … गुरुदंडांश् च पुष्कतान्), and other heavenly missiles (like वज्राणि and चक्राणि) out of the bones of the sage Dadhīca 9. 50. 30; Śiva is called the creator of the Brahmadaṇḍa (ब्रह्म-दण्डविनिर्माता) 13. 17. 130. B. Asso-ciations: (1) It was looked upon as a weapon specially of Yama (cf. the expression Yama-daṇḍa in section C below); hence Yama called ‘holding दण्ड in hand’ (दण्डपाणि) 3. 12. 46; 3. 42. 10; (दण्डहस्त) 8. 29. 28 (Vaivasvata); (दण्डधार) 3. 40. 38; or ‘equipped with Daṇḍa’ (दण्डिन्) 1. 180. 16; it was Yama who gave his irresistible (अप्रतिवारण) Daṇḍa to Arjuna with proper rites (विधिवत्), together with the मन्त्रस् (समन्त्रम्), and instruction regarding its full operation (सोपचारम् = सेतिकर्तव्यता-कम् according to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 41. 26), its release (समोक्षम्), and withdrawal (सनिवर्तनम्); Arjuna was supposed to perform great deeds with it 3. 42. 23-24; 3. 89. 12; 4. 56. 14; 7. 53. 43; 12. 5. 13; Yama held it (कालदण्ड) when he wished to fight with Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna at the time of the Khāṇḍava fire 1. 218. 31, 37; some people afraid to commit sins due to their fear of Yama's Daṇḍa 12. 15. 5; (a king punish-ing the unrighteous with दण्ड (punish-ment) acts like Yama 12. 68. 45); (2) of Antaka (cf. the expression Antaka-daṇḍa in section C below); hence Antaka called दण्डपाणि 4. 22. 19; 5. 50. 7; 6. 50. 2; 6. 58. 51; 6. 59. 11; 6. 78. 57; 6. 103. 68; 8. 43. 70; 9. 18. 46; 9. 24. 28; दण्डहस्त 2. 72. 31; 6. 98. 35; 7. 14. 5; 7. 131. 30; 9. 25. 2; 9. 31. 39; (3) of Mṛtyu (cf. the expression Mṛtyudaṇḍa in section C below) who is equipped with fierce Daṇḍa 1. 167. 19; (4) of Kāla (cf. the expression Kāladaṇḍa in section C below); Kāla called ‘equipped with दण्ड’ (दण्डिन्) 9. 60. 60; Yama held कालदण्ड 1. 218. 31; Antaka held कालदण्ड 7. 107. 87; (5) of Brahman (cf. the expression Brahmadaṇḍa in section C below); angry Sudhanvan compar-ed with the burning Brahmadaṇḍa 2. 61. 62; Vāsuki, afraid of his mother's curse, confused the directions as though he was tormented by Brahmadaṇḍa 1. 49. 22; Āstīka would destroy the Brahmadaṇḍa (महाघोर) of which Vāsuki was so much afraid 1. 49. 24; serpents, struck by Brahmadaṇḍa, fell into the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 22; Brahmadaṇḍa mentioned among the missiles which should be known to a king 2. 5. 111; Brahmadaṇḍa and other missiles moved around the chariot of Śiva (परिस्कन्दाः) to guard it in all directions 8. 24. 79; (6) of Rudra: Rudradaṇḍa among those missiles which moved round the chariot of Śiva (परिस्कन्दाः) to guard it in all directions 8. 24. 29. C. Comparisons: Missiles like arrows, गदा, शक्ति, or even a tree or a stick used as a powerful weapon, compar-ed with the दण्ड (Yamadaṇḍa, Antakadaṇḍa, Mṛtyudaṇḍa, Kāladaṇḍa or Brahmadaṇḍa): (a) arrows: (1) of Droṇa compared with Yamadaṇḍa 6. 102. 5 (शित); with Kāla-daṇḍa 6. 43. 30 (महाघोर); with Mṛtyu-daṇḍa 6. 49. 9; with Brahmadaṇḍa 7. 164. 122; (2) of Arjuna compared with Yamadaṇḍa 6. 106. 39 (घोर); 9. 26. 42 (शित); with Antakadaṇḍa 8. 66. 31; with Brahmadaṇḍa 6. 114. 57; (3) of Bhīma compared with Mṛtyudaṇḍa 6. 76. 5 (घोर); with Yamadaṇḍa 9. 25. 22 (शुभ ‘shin-ing’ ?); 7. 108. 25; (4) of Karṇa compared with Mṛtyudaṇḍa 8. 42. 12; (5) of Aśvatthāman compared with Yamadaṇḍa 7. 141. 34 (घोर); 9. 13. 38 (तीक्ष्ण); with Antakadaṇḍa 8. 15. 39; (6) of Sātyaki compared with Yamadaṇḍa 6. 70. 20 (घोर); 7. 92. 38; (7) of Jaya-dratha compared with Yamadaṇḍa 6. 81. 30; (8) of Abhimanyu compared with Yamadaṇḍa 6. 96. 4 (घोर); (9) of Alaṃbusa compared with Yamadaṇḍa 6. 97. 18 (शित); (10) of Nakula compared with Yamadaṇḍa 8. 17. 15; (11) of Sahadeva compared with Yamadaṇḍa 8. 17. 38 (त्विष्); (12) of Śrutarvan compared with Yama-daṇḍa 9. 25. 22 (शुभ ‘shining’ ?); (13) of Rāma compared with Brahmadaṇḍa 3. 274. 27; (b) गदा: (1) of Bhīma compared with Yamadaṇḍa 3. 152. 15 (गुर्वी); 6. 58. 57 (गुर्वी); 6. 59. 16 (उग्रा); 6. 81. 33; 6. 90. 21 (गुर्वी); 9. 10. 43; 9. 56. 12 (गुर्वी, रौद्री, विशसनी); 9. 56. 24-25 (गुर्वी, घोरा); compared with the Daṇḍa of Antaka 2. 72. 31; 5. 50. 7 (घोरा); 6. 50. 2; 6. 58. 51; 6. 59. 11 (गुर्वी, महती); 6. 78. 57; 9. 18. 46 (महती); 9. 24. 28 (महती); 9. 25. 2 (गदा not mentioned); compared with the Daṇḍa of Kāla 7. 102. 87; 7. 104. 3; 7. 170. 46; with the Daṇḍa of Brahman 5. 50. 8; (2) of Dhṛṣṭadyumna compared with Yamadaṇḍa 6. 112. 47; (3) of Duryodhana: Duryodhana with his गदा compared with Antaka holding दण्ड 9. 31. 39; Duryodhana with his गदा in hand cannot be killed even by Kāla armed with his Daṇḍa (कालेनापीह दण्डिना) 9. 60. 60; (4) Śalya with his गदा compared with Antaka holding दण्ड 7. 14. 5; (c) शक्ति: (1) of Rāma Jāmadagnya compared with Yamadaṇḍa 5. 185. 5 (प्रभा); (2) of Bhagadatta compared with Yamadaṇḍa 6. 107. 11 (दृढा, घोरा); (3) of Yudhi-ṣṭhira compared with Brahmadaṇḍa 9. 16. 42 (उग्ररूपा); (d) शूल: of Rāvaṇa hurled against Rāma compared with Brahmadaṇḍa 3. 274. 19; cut off by Rāma 3. 274. 20; (e) तोमर: Naiṣādi (not identified) armed with तोमर compared with Antaka holding the दण्ड 8. 43. 70; (f) Bow: (1) Ghaṭotkaca with bow in his hand compared with Antaka holding दण्ड in his hand 7. 131. 30; with Antaka holding Kāladaṇḍa in hand 7. 150. 33 (उग्र); (2) Aśvatthāman (bow not mentioned) compared with Kāla holding Daṇḍa 5. 164. 10; (g) a tusk of an elephant: Bhīma holding a tusk compared with Antaka holding his Daṇḍa 6. 98. 35; (h) a tree or a stick: (1) the tree held by Bhīma compared with the Daṇḍa of Yama (Pitṛrāja) 1. 180. 16 (उग्र); the tree of Bhīma to fight with Kirmīra compared with Yamadaṇḍa 3. 12. 43; Bhīma with tree in hand compared with Antaka holding his Daṇḍa 4. 22. 19; (2) the tree of Kirmīra compared with the Daṇḍa of Yama (not named) 3. 12. 46; (3) King Kalmāṣapāda with stick (काष्ठ) in hand compared with Mṛtyu holding Daṇḍa 1. 167. 19 (उग्र); (4) the stick (दण्ड) held by Ruru compared with Kāladaṇḍa 1. 9. 21; (5) the त्रिदण्ड held by Śunaḥsakha compared with Brahmadaṇḍa 13. 95. 48; (6) Garuḍa: compared with a raised Brahmadaṇḍa 1. 26. 7. [See Kiṃkara]
देवदत्त: Devadatta m.: Name of Arjuna's conch. A. Origin: Produced in water जलो-द्भव 3. 165. 22; वारिज 3. 172. 5. B. Description: Heavenly (दिव्य) 5. 47. 58; 6. 1. 17; 6. 23. 14; excellent conch, excellent among all conches, unsurpassed (शङ्ख-प्रवर) 3. 165. 21; (शङ्खवर) 6. 47. 25; (सर्वशङ्खवर) 7. 79. 11; (अनुत्तम) 2. 3. 18; of large size (महाशङ्ख) 2. 3. 7; 7. 18. 10; frightful (भीम) 8. 54. 27; shining white like snow (हिमावदात) 8. 68. 56, or shining like a white cloud (पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाश) 8. 54. 27; producing loud sound (महास्वन) 3. 166. 11; 8. 68. 56; (महारव) 3. 171. 5, or good sound (सुघोष) 8. 54. 27; 8. 68. 55; (सुघोषवन्त्) 2. 3. 7; decorated with gold (हेमपरिष्कृत) 7. 17. 8, with golden net (सुवर्णजालावतत) 8. 68. 56, or with gold and jewels (हेम-रत्नपरिष्कृत) 6. 47. 24. C. History: It belonged to Varuṇa (वारुण); Maya brought it from Bindusaras for Arjuna 2. 3. 7, 16, 18; but according to another tradition it was in the possession of Indra and he conquered the worlds with it; it was given by the gods to Arjuna when he was to leave for his battle with the Nivātakavacas 3. 165. 21, 22; God (Indra) gifted it to Arjuna when he returned victorious from his fight with the Nivātakavacas and the Kāla-keyas 3. 171. 5; 8. 57. 43. D. Effect of its sound: When blown by Arjuna its sound filled the space and reached up to the heaven 3. 166. 12; 7. 17. 8; 7. 79. 12; 8. 68. 57; it terrified the minds of the enemies (but caused delight to the friends) 6. 23. 19; 4. 61. 28; 8. 68. 57; hearing it the enemies and the horses yoked to their chariots ejected urine and excreta 6. 1. 18; or, hearing it the army of the opponents became stupefied and the horses ejected urine and blood 7. 17. 9-10, the elephants became distracted (विचेतसः) and slower in movement (मन्दवेगतराः) 7. 65. 15; even big creatures were frightened to hear the sound and they lay low (वित्रेसुश् च निलिल्युश् च भूतानि सुमहान्त्य् अपि) 3. 166. 12. E. Use: Having received Devadatta, Arjuna kept it on his chariot (along with his bow and the quivers) 5. 47. 58; 8. 54. 27; he must have blown it on all important occasions; specific mention of the blowing is found: (1) when Arjuna attacked the city of the Nivātakavacas 3. 166. 11; when he got ready to demonstrate his acquisition of the divine weapons to his brothers 3. 172. 5; when Arjuna defeated the Kaurava heroes at the time of the cattle-raid 4. 61. 28; when the two armies of the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas were arrayed against each other 6. 1. 17-18; 6. 23. 15; 6. 47. 25; while fighting with the Saṃśaptakas 7. 17. 8; 7. 18. 10; 8. 37. 19; when Arjuna took the vow to kill Jayadratha 7. 51. 41; while fighting with the elephants of Duḥśāsana 7. 65. 14; while fighting with the warriors who protected Jayadratha 7. 79. 11; when he succeeded in killing Karṇa 8. 68. 57.
दैतेयास्त्र: Daiteyāstra nt.: Name (?) of a missile. The terrible माया of the Asuras (आसुरीं दारुणीं मायाम्), employed by Śālva against Pradyumna, so called; with its employment Śālva was able to shoot at once a number of arrows; the missile was successfully cut down half way by Pradyumna by using Brahmāstra 3. 20. 16-18.
दिग्विजय: Digvijaya m.: Name of the 23rd पर्-वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 40, 33, 70. Referred to in Sūta's summary of the events for the sages assembled in the Naimiṣa forest 1. 1. 84; also in Vaiśaṃpāyana's summary of the events for Janamejaya 1. 55. 28, 29; related to the अध्यायस् 2. 23-29.
दैवतवंश: Daivatavaṃśa m.: Name of a passage in the Anuśasanaparvan listing the names of gods, goddesses, and other beings (अयं दैवतवंशो वै) 13. 151. 2. Besides listing names of gods like Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) with Sāvitrī, Viṣṇu-Nārāyaṇa, Umāpati (Śiva), Virūpā-kṣa, Skanda, Viśākha and others, it contains also such names like Surabhi (cow), Sāgara (ocean), and Gaṅgā (river); it has names of sages like the Vālakhilyas, Kṛṣṇa-dvai-pāyana, Nārada and Parvata; of Gandhar-vas like Viśvāvasu Hahāhuhū and others; of Apsarases like Urvaśī, Menakā, Rambhā and others; it mentions also group-gods like the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Aśvinā, and also the Pitṛs; personified concepts like धर्म, सत्य; divisions of time like nights and days, seasons, months, twilights; names of planets (Śukra, Brhaspati and the rest) and Nakṣatras (not listed); mythical birds (Vainateyas) and serpents (कद्रुजाः); rivers like Śatadrū, Vipāśā and others; holy places of pilgrimage like Prayāga, Prabhāsa and others; mountains like Himavant, Vindhya and the rest—all these also find a place in this list 13. 151. 3-28; together with the Ṛṣivaṃśa, this Daivata-vaṃśa is described as the ‘first collection’ of its kind (एष वै समवायस् ते ऋषि-देवसमन्वितः । आद्यः प्रकीर्तितो राजन्) 13. 151. 40; also अयं दैवतवंशो वै ऋषिवंशसमन्वितः 13. 151. 2; the recita-tion of the two वंशस् together at two twilights is very effective in removing sins (द्विसंध्यं पठितः पुत्र कल्माषा-पहरः परः) 13. 151. 2; (सर्वपाप-प्रमोचनः) 13. 151. 40; (मुच्यते सर्व-किल्बिशैः) 13. 151. 29; one who recites these names of gods or welcomes their recitation is freed of dangers from all quarters and from sins arising from all kinds of promis-cuous behaviour (स्तुवंश् च प्रतिनन्दंश् च मुच्यते सर्वतो भयात् । सर्वसंकर-पापेभ्यो देवतास्तवनन्दकः ॥ ) 13. 151. 29. [See Ṛṣivaṃśa]
द्यूतपर्वन्: Dyūtaparvan nt.: Name of the 27th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 41, 33, 70. The incidents of this पर्वन् briefly listed in the contents of the Sabhāparvan (1. 2. 100-102): Bhīma derided Duryodhana in the Sabhā; the game of dice traced to the wrath of Duryodhana aroused due to his derision by Bhīma; in the द्यूत that followed, Śakuni defeated Dharmasuta (Yudhiṣṭhira); Draupadī came to their rescue; referred to also by Dhṛtaraṣṭra in his summary made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 99-100; 105-106; and still more briefly by Vaiśaṃpāyana in his summary for Janamejaya 1. 55. 39; related to the अध्यायस् 2. 43-65.
द्रोणपर्वन्: Droṇaparvan nt.: Name of the 7th पर्वन् in the list of the 18 major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 160, 166, 233. Described as wonderful and full of in-cidents (चित्रम्, बहुवृत्तान्तम्) 1. 2. 160, great (महत्) 1. 2. 166; most of the heroic kings were killed in the Droṇaparvan 1. 2. 66; the main incidents in this पर्वन् are listed as follows: the Saṃśaptakas removed Arjuna from the main battle-field; Bhagadatta, with his elephant Supratīka, killed by Arjuna; young Abhimanyu killed by many heroes who were led by Jayadratha; angered Arjuna killed seven Akṣauhiṇīs and Jayadratha; all the Saṃśaptakas destroyed without a re-mainder; Alambusa, Śrutāyus, Jalasaṃdha, Saumadatti, Virāṭa, Drupada, Ghaṭotkaca and many others killed in this पर्वन्; Aśvatthāman, enraged at the fall of Droṇa, released his frightful Nārāyaṇāstra 1. 2. 160-165; the अध्यायस् of the Droṇaparvan, as counted by Vyāsa, the seer of truth (तत्त्व-दर्शिना) after due thought (संचिन्त्य) are 170 and its श्लोकस् 8909 (1. 2. 167-168).
द्रोणवध: Droṇavadha m.: Name of the 71st पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 58, 33, 70. Described as hair-raising (लोमहर्-षण) 1. 2. 58; fall of Droṇa referred to while listing the major events of the Droṇa-parvan 1. 2. 165, and in the summary of the events made by Dhṛtarāṣṭra for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 143; the पर्वन् is related to the inci-dents narrated in the अध्यायस् 7. 155 (or 159)-165.
द्रोणाभिषेक: Droṇābhiṣeka m.: Name of the 65th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 56, 33, 70. Related to the अध्यायस् 7. 1-15 (7. 5. 5-40).
द्रौपदीसत्यभामयोः: Draupadīsatyabhāmayoḥ saṃvādaḥ: Name of the 38th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parva-saṃgraha (संवादश् च ततः पर्व द्रौ-पदीसत्यभामयोः) 1. 2. 45, 33, 70. The incident is mentioned while listing the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan (संवादश् चैव सत्यया) 1. 2. 125; the पर्वन् is related to the अध्यायस् 3. 222-224.
द्रौपदीस्वयंवर: Draupadīsvayaṃvara m.: This name does not occur in the text. [See Pāñcālyāḥ svayaṃvaram] Related to the अध्यायस् 1. 174-189.
द्रौपदीहरण: Draupadīharaṇa nt.: Name of the 42nd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 47, 33, 70. Draupadī's abduction was attempted by the Sindhu king (Jayadratha) 1. 2. 47; the incident is mentioned while listing the con-tents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 123-124; the पर्वन् is related to the incidents of the अध्यायस् 3. 248-256.
दक्षिणायन: Dakṣiṇāyana nt.: Name of the period of six months in which the sun moves towards the south (also expressed as दक्षिणावृत्त आदित्ये 6. 114. 96). A. Duration: It lasts for six months (षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम्) 6. 30. 25. B. Association with darkness: Vyāsa told Śuka that Dakṣiṇāyaṇa formed the night of the gods (रात्रिः स्याद् दक्षिणायनम्) 12. 224. 16; Dakṣiṇāyana is associated with blind darkness and the dark night (अन्धं तमस् तमिस्रं च दक्षिणायनम् एव च) 13. 101. 46. C. Bhīṣma's falling down in the Dakṣiṇāyana and his death in the Uttarā-yaṇa: When Bhīṣma fell down on the battle-field he heard a heavenly voice in the mid-region resounding all around saying “how should the high-souled Gāṅgeya (Bhīṣma) die when it was Dakṣiṇāyana ?” (कथं महात्मा गाङ्गेयः … । कालं कर्ता नर-व्याघ्रः संप्राप्ते दक्षिणायने) 6. 114. 88; the great sages who, in the form of the swans, were sent by Gaṅgā observed that the sun was in the south when Bhīṣma fell from the chariot (दक्षिणेन च भास्करम् 6. 114. 93); they said to each other: (it seems) Bhīṣma, though high-souled, shall die when it was Dakṣiṇāyaṇa (इतरेतरम् आमन्त्र्य प्राहुस् तत्र मनीषिणः । भीष्म एव महा-त्मा सन् संस्थाता दक्षिणायने ॥ ) 6. 114. 94 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 119. 102: सं-स्थाता मरिष्यति); Bhīṣma then assured the sages that he had resolved that in no case would he go (from this world) when the sun was turned towards the south (तान् अब्रवीच् छान्तनवो नाहं गन्ता कथं-चन । दक्षिणावृत्त आदित्ये एतन् मे मनसि स्थितम् ॥ ) 6. 114. 96; Yudhiṣṭhira became anxious when the realized that Bhīṣma had only a few days to live in the Dakṣiṇāyana and that he would soon leave for the highest state when the sun had started moving (north-wards) (शेषम् अल्पं द्मानां ते दक्षिणा-यनभास्करे । आवृत्ते भगवत्य् अर्के गन्त्-आसि परमां गतिम् ॥ ) 12. 291. 4; the period of Dakṣiṇāyaṇa, when Bhīṣma fell, is alluded to in Bhīṣma's instruction to Yudhiṣṭhira to come back to him when the sun had return-ed (from the southerly course) (विनिवृत्ते दिनकरे) 13. 152. 10; it is also alluded to when Yudhiṣṭhira returned to meet Bhīṣma (दृष्ट्वा निवृत्तम् आदित्यम् प्रवृत्तं चोत्तरा-यणम्) 13. 153. 6; when Bhīṣma, on seeing Yudhiṣṭhira, greeted him and said that the sun had, indeed, returned (from the southerly course) (परिवृत्तो हि भगवान् सहस्रांशुर् दिवाकरः) 13. 153. 26; and when Bhīṣma, composed in attitude, put his entire bodily function in his self as soon as the sun had returned (from the south) (निवृत्तमात्रे त्व् अयने उत्तरे वै दिवाकरे । समावेशयद् आत्मानम् आत्मन्य् एव समाहितः ॥ ) 12. 47. 3; Bhīṣma finally died when the sun left the southerly course and the Uttarāyaṇa had start-ed (अकरोत् स ततः कालं शरतल्पगतो मुनिः ॥ अयनं दक्षिणं हित्वा संप्राप्ते चोत्तरायणे ॥ ) 14. 59. 12. D. Death in the Dakṣiṇāyana: If a Yogī dies during the six months of the Dakṣiṇāyana he, after reaching the moon's realm of light, returns to this world (षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् । तत्र चान्-द्रमसं ज्योतिर् योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥ ) 6. 30. 25; Nārada, while consoling Sṛñjaya lamenting over the death of his son, told him that Ambarīṣa, son of Nābhāga, and hundreds of other kings who performed the Aśvamedha, went towards the Dakṣiṇāyana (i. e. died during the Dakṣiṇāyana) (सर्वे ऽश्वमेधैर् ईजानास् ते ऽभ्ययुर् दक्षिणाय-नम्) 12. 29. 96; (Nī., however, who reads अन्वयुः, on Bom. Ed. 12. 29. 103: सर्वे राजानः … दक्षिणायनम् अनु पश्चात् अयुर् गताः । उत्तरायणमार्गेण हिरण्यगर्भ-लोकं प्राप्ताः इत्य् अर्थः); but men who perform bad deeds and who die in the Dakṣiṇāyana wait upon Dharmarāja (Yama) in his सभा (नरा दुष्कृतकर्माणो दक्षि-णायनमृत्यवः । … उपासते धर्मराजम्) 2. 8. 28-29. [For most of the information which is common to both the अयनस् the Uttara and the Dakṣiṇa, see Uttarāyaṇa].
द्वापर: Dvāpara m., nt.: Name of the third Yuga among the four Yugas. A. Place among the four Yugas: Its place is third, mentioned after the Tretā and before the Kali (कृतं त्रेता द्वा-परं च पुष्यं च कुरुवर्धन) 6. 11. 3; 12. 224. 18; the Dvāpara starts when the Tretā ends (त्रेतानिर्मोक्षसमये द्वापरप्रतिपादने) 12. 139. 14; and the Kali starts when the Dvāpara ends (सङ्क्षेपाद् द्वापरस्याथ ततः पुष्यं प्रवर्तते) 6. 11. 4; hence also the junctions of the Tretā and the Dvāpara on the one hand and of the Dvāpara and the Kali on the other are referred to 1. 2. 3; 12. 139. 13; 12. 326. 78; 1. 2. 9; 12. 326. 82. B. Duration: Mārkaṇḍeya told Yudhiṣṭhira that the duration of the Dvāpara Yuga was two thousand years with dawns and twilights of two hundred years each at both ends (तथा वर्षसहस्रे द्वे द्वापरं परिमाणतः । तस्यापि द्विशती संध्या संध्यांशस् च ततः परम् ॥ संध्यासंध्यांशयोस् तुल्-यं प्रमाणम् उपधारय) 3. 186. 20-21 (for Nī's explanation of संध्या and संध्यांश see above Kali, section C, p. 234); the same duration for the Dvāpara was told by Vyāsa to Śuka without naming the Yuga, but indicating it in relation to the Kṛta 12. 224. 20. C. Events occurring in the Dvāpara: (1) Bhīṣma told Yudhi-ṣṭhira that formerly, at the junction of the Tretā and the Dvāpara, there occurred a terrible drought lasting for twelve years due to the working of the fate (दैवविधि-क्रमात्); when the Tretā was about to end and the Dvāpara was to set in Indra did not release rain for twelve years (त्रेतानिर्-मोक्षसमये द्वापरप्रतिपादने ॥ न ववर्ष सहस्राक्षः) 12. 139. 13-15; (2) Sūta Ugraśravas told the sages assembled in the Naimiṣa forest that at the junction of the Tretā and the Dvāpara (त्रेताद्वापरयोः संधौ) Rāma destroyed the princely Kṣatriyas again and again 1. 2. 3 (but see the next event); (3) Bhagavān (Nārā-yaṇa) told Nārada that at the junction of the Tretā and the Dvāpara (संधौ तु समनुप्राप्ते त्रेतायां द्वापरस्य च) he would be born as Rāma, son of Daśaratha 12. 326. 78; (4) Bhagavān (Nārāyaṇa) told Nārada that towards the end of the junction of the Dvāpara and the Kali (द्वापरस्य कलेश् चैव संधौ पर्यव-सानिके) he would be born in Mathurā for (the killing of) Kaṃsa 12. 326. 82; (5) at the junction of the Dvāpara and the Kali the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas fought each other near Samantapañcaka 1. 2. 9. D. Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) and the Dvāpara: (1) Bhagavān (Nārāyaṇa) told Mārka-ṇḍeya that he has red colour in the Dvāpara Yuga (रक्तो द्वापरम् आसाद्य) 3. 187. 31; but according to Hanūmant Viṣṇu becomes yellow in the Dvāpara (द्वापरे ऽपि युगे … विष्णुर् वै पीततां याति) 3. 148. 26; (3) Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that Kṛṣṇa was strength in the Dvāpara (बलं त्व् आसीद् द्वा-परे पार्थ कृष्णः) 13. 143. 9. E. King and the Dvāpara: According to Utathya Aṅgiras all the four Yugas depend on the king's behaviour, hence a king himself is called Yuga (राजवृत्तानि सर्वाणि राजैव युगम् उच्यते) 12. 92. 6; Bhīṣma had no doubt that all the Yugas were rooted in a king (राजमूलानि सर्वाणि मम नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः) 12. 139. 10; it is the king who created a Yuga—whether it was the Kṛta, the Tretā, or the Dvāpara 5. 130. 16 = 12. 70. 25 (also cf. राजा कालस्य कारणम् 5. 130. 15 = 12. 70. 6); when a king gives up half of the दण्डनीति and practises only one half of it, then the Dvāpara age sets in (अर्धं त्यक्त्वा यदा राजा नीत्यर्धम् अनुवर्तते । ततस् तु द्वापरं नाम स कालः संप्रवर्तते ॥ ) 12. 70. 16; the धर्म practised by the king in the Dvāpara is deficient in two quarters (द्वापरे तु द्विपादेन (ऊनः)) 12. 259. 32; by bringing about the Dvāpara a king lives in heaven only according to his share (i. e. not for a long time) (प्रवर्तनाद् द्वापरस्य (स्वर्गम्) यथाभागम् य्पाश्नुते) 5. 130. 17 = 12. 70. 27; (description of the behaviour of people in the Dvāpara in the absence of the दण्डनीति 12. 65. 24-27). F. Dvāpara and धर्म: In the Dvāpara Yuga, धर्म will lose two of its four feet and the age will be marked by a mixture (of धर्म and अधर्म) (ततो वै द्वापरं नाम मिश्रः कालो भविष्यति । द्विपादहीनो धर्मश् च युगे तस्मिन् भविष्यति) 12. 327. 75; (द्वापरे ऽर्धेन व्यामिश्रो धर्म उच्यते) 3. 188. 11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 190. 10: अर्धेन अधर्मेण); (अशुभस्य तदा अर्धं द्वाव् अंशाव् अनुवर्तते) 12. 70. 17; (द्वापरे ऽपि युगे धर्मो द्विभागोनः प्रवर्तते) 3. 148. 26; 12. 259. 32; in the Yugas that follow the Kṛta the traditional धर्म is displaced successively by one quarter and in-stead अधर्म increases due to the practice of theft, falsehood and deceit 12. 224. 23; the धर्मस् in the Dvāpara are different from those in the Kṛta and the Tretā 12. 224. 26 = 12. 252. 8; according to Mārkaṇḍeya, however, the धर्म for the Kṛta, the Tretā and the Dvāpara was the same (एष ढर्मः कृत-युगे त्रेतायां द्वापरे तथा) 3. 189. 13; sacrifice was considered to be the best धर्म for the Dvāpara (द्वापरे यज्ञम् एवाहुः (उत्तमम्)) 12. 224. 27; Hanūmant told Bhīma that the times in different Yugas were different; he and Bhīma lived at a time when the Dvāpara was about to end and hence he could not assume the form he had taken in the earlier Yuga (अयं प्रध्वंसनः कालो नाद्य तद् रूपम् अस्ति मे) 3. 148. 6; Kṛṣṇa-Vāsudeva, along with Saṃkaraṣṇa, is praised following the Sātvata rites when the Dvāpara ends, and the Kali begins (द्वाप-रस्य युगस्यान्ते आदौ कलियुगस्य च । सात्वतं विधिं आस्थाय गीतः संकर्षणेन यः (i. e. कृष्णः) 6. 62. 39. G. Dvāpara, sacrifice and the Vedas: Vyāsa told his son Śuka that on account of the limitation on the life expectancy (of human beings) sacrifices, in the Dvāparayuga, get into disarray (संर्च्-धाद् आयुषस् त्व् एते (i. e. यज्ञाः) व्यस्यन्ते द्वापरे युगे) 12. 224. 65 = 12. 230. 14; they fall into ruin (द्वापरे विप्लवं यान्ति यज्ञाः) 12. 224. 62 = 12. 230. 15 (विप्लवं यान्ति वेदाः); however, sacrifice considered to be the best धर्म for the Dvāpara (द्वापरे यज्ञम् एवाहुः (उत्तमम्) 12. 224. 27; Hanūmant told Bhīma that in the Dvāpara the Veda is foretold; hence some study all the four Vedas, others three, two, or one; but some do not study a single ऋच्; as men did not realize the sacred text to be one Veda, the Veda was divided into many (Vedas) (द्वापरे ऽपि युगे … चतुर्धा वेद एव च ॥ ततो ऽन्ये च चतुर्वेदास् त्रिवेदाश् च तथापरे । द्विवेदाश् चैकवेदाश्-चाप्य् अनृचश् च तथापरे ॥ … एकवेदस्य चाज्ञानाद् वेदास् ते बहवः कृताः) 3. 148. 26-27, 29 (Nī., on Bom. Ed. 3. 149. 28, offers an alternative explanation: यद् वा चतुर्वेदा इति वेदत्रयोक्तं कर्म ज्योतिष्टो-मादिकम् । अथर्वणोपनिषदुक्तम् ध्या-नं च सहैव वानुतिष्ठन्तीति कर्मोपास्ति-समुच्चय उक्तः । त्रिवेदा इति केवलकर्-मठाः । द्विवेदा इति स्वशाखोक्तं सं-ध्यावन्दनादि कर्म ध्यानं चानुति-ष्ठन्ति । एकवेदा ध्यानैकनिष्ठाः॑ अनृचः कृतकृत्याः । ); (also cf. Maheśvara (Viṣṇu) recommending the performance of sacrifices to satisfy the gods and the gods, on their part, sustaining the worlds in the (three) Yugas other than the Kṛta 12. 327. 53-60). H. Nature: According to the description of the Dvāpara given by Hanū-mant to Bhīma, since in that age the Vedas become fourfold and the शास्त्रस् multiply, the Vedic rites are variously performed; people, given to austerities and gifts, become राजस by nature; since truth falls down, rarely any one abides by truth (एवं शास्त्रेषु भिन्नेषु बहुधा नियते कृइया । तपोदानप्रवृत्ता च राजसी भवति प्रजा ॥  … सत्यस्य चेह विभ्रंशात् सत्ये कश्चिद् अवस्थितः ॥ ) 3. 148. 28-29; for further description of the Dvāpara cf. 3. 148. 30-31; Hanūmant concludes that people in the Dvāpara perish due to the practice of अधर्म (एवं द्वापरम् आसाद्य प्रजाः क्षीयन्त्य् अधर्मतः) 3. 148. 32; according to Saṃjaya, in the Dvāpara all the four वर्णस् are full of energy; they are great heroes, desirous of killing each other; on the whole, the Dvāpara in which Saṃjaya lived was characterized by contraction (of the me-rits in all respects) (सर्ववर्णा महाराज जायन्ते द्वापरे सति । महोत्साहा महावीर्-याः परस्परवधैषिणः ॥ … संक्षेपो वर्तते राजन् द्वापरे ऽस्मिन् नराधिप) 6. 11. 11, 14 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 10. 15: संक्षेपो गुणानाम् इति शेषः); Vyāsa told Śuka that all the वर्णस् and the आश्रमस् fall into disarray due to the limitation on the life-span (वर्णाश्रमास् तथा । संर्च्-धाद् आयुषस् त्व् एते व्यस्यन्ते द्वापरे युगे) 12. 230. 14; he also said that people in the Dvāpara (as in the Tretā and the Kali) entertain doubt (त्रेतायां द्वापरे चैव कलिजाश् च ससंशयाः 12. 230. 7) as to what is at the root of a man's success— his effort, fate, or nature 12. 230. 4; in the Dvāpara, the earth has to be ploughed and even then it does not yield much harvest (कृष्टपच्यैव पृथिवी भवत्य् अल्पफला तथा) 12. 70. 17; in this Yuga people have to copulate to beget progeny (द्वापरे मैथुनो धर्मः प्रजानाम् अभवन् नृप) 12. 200. 37; evil tribes like the Talavaras and the Andharkas from the south and the Yaunas (Yavanas) and the Gāndhāras from the north move on earth from the Tretā onwards (i. e. also in the Dvāpara) 12. 200. 39-40, 42. I. Life expectancy: Vyāsa told his son Śuka that the life expectancy of people dimini-shes by a quarter in each succeeding Yuga after the Kṛta, hence in the Dvāpara they live for two hundred years ( … त्रेतादिष्व् एतेषां पादशो ह्रसते वयः) 12. 224. 24; Vyāsa also told Śuka that according to his information life expectancy of people, along with other things, gradually decreased in the successive Yugas ( … अनुयुगं ह्रसन्तीति च नः श्रुतम् । आयूंषि … ) 12. 224. 25; this is also what Mārkaṇḍeya told Yudhi-ṣṭhira (आयुर् … मनुष्याणाम् अनुयुगं ह्रसतीति निबोध मे) 3. 188. 13; according to Saṃjaya, however, the life expectancy of people in the Dvāpara was two thousand years (आयुःसंख्या … संक्त्याता … । द्वि-सहस्रं द्वापरे तु) 6. 11. 5-6 (ap-parently Saṃjaya made confusion between the duration of the Dvāpara age and the life expectancy of people in that Yuga). J. Simile: The place where the river Narmadā passes along the Vaiḍūrya moun-tain is compared to the junction of the Tretā (f.) and the Dvāpara (m.) 3. 121. 18-19. K. Name of Sūrya: Dvāpara appears as 48th name among the hundred and eight names of Sūrya taught by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 22. [The words कृत, त्रेता, द्वापर and कलि occurring in 5. 140. 7-15 are wrongly interpreted by Nīlakaṇṭha (Bom. Ed. 5. 142. 7-15) as names of the four Yugas, and not as the names of the throws in the game of dice].
दक्षिणसिन्धु: *Dakṣiṇasindhu m.: Name of a river, the Sindhu of the south. One should visit the Dakṣiṇasindhu after visiting Narmadā, and from there proceed to Carmaṇvatī 3. 80. 71-73; One who observes chastity and has controlled his senses obtains, by visiting the southern Sindhu, the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and rides in a विमान (दक्षिणं सिन्धुम् आसाद्य … विमानं चाधिरोहति) 3. 80. 72.
दण्डक: Daṇḍaka (m. ?), Daṇḍakāraṇya nt.: Name of a forest and a तीर्थ। A. Location: The river Godāvarī flew through it 3. 261. 40; the आश्रम of Śara-bhaṅga was in this forest 3. 261. 39. B. Description: Large forest (महावन) 9. 38. 10; (महारण्य) 3. 261. 39; (वने महति) 3. 263. 24; holy forest (धर्मारण्य) 3. 261. 43. C. Holy तीर्थ: One should bathe there (उपस्पृशेत्); just by bathing there (स्नातमात्रस्य) one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 83. 38. D. Rāmāyaṇa events: (1) Rāma, during the term of his exile, lived there with his wife and brother on the river Godāvarī 3. 147. 29; 3. 261. 40; (2) Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa proceeded towards its south in search of Sītā 3. 263. 23; (3) There they encountered Kabandha 3. 263. 25; (4) Rāghava killed Khara, Dūṣaṇa and other fourteen thousand demons and made the holy forest safe again (चक्रे क्षेमं पुनर् धीमान् धर्मारण्यं स राघवः) 3. 261. 43; 9. 38. 9. E. Past events: (1) “The fire of the anger of sages who blazed with austerities is not extinguished even now in the Daṇḍaka” said the wife of the Brāh-maṇa to Kauśika (तथैव दीप्ततपसां मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम् । येषां क्रोधाग्निर् अद्यापि दण्डके नोपशाम्यति ॥ ) 3. 197. 25 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 206. 27 has simply दण्डके दण्डकारण्ये); 13. 136. 17; (2) “A certain Brāhmaṇa destroyed the kingdom of the Daṇḍakas.”—this is what Vāyu told Sahasrārjuna (दण्डकानां महद् राज्यं ब्राह्मणेन विनाशितम्) 13. 138. 11.

Daṇḍaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: South: they were en-countered by Sahadeva in the south (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1, 8, 37; B. Epic event: They were subjugated by Sahadeva in his expedition before the Rājasūya (वशे चक्रे … दण्डकांश् च महाबलः) 2. 28. 43; C. Past event: Their large kingdom was destroyed by a Brāhmaṇa 13. 138. 11.
दण्डार्क: Daṇḍārka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in Campā, near the river Bhāgīrathī; one who bathes in the Bhāgīrathī (भागीरथ्यां कृतोदकः) and just visits the Daṇḍārka (दण्डार्कम् अभिगम्यैव) gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 82. 142.
दधिमण्डोदक: Dadhimaṇḍodaka m.: Name of an ocean. One of the four oceans around the northern Dvīpas; apparently its water was all whey (उत्तरेषु तु कौरव्य द्वीपेषु … दधिमण्डोदको ऽपरः) 6. 13. 1-2.
दधीचस्य: Dadhīcasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as most holy (पुण्यतम), purifying (पावन) and famous in the worlds (लोकविश्रुत); Aṅgiras Sārasvata is present there; one who bathes in this तीर्थ gets the fruit of a Vājapeya and secures for himself, without any doubt, the state which will be reached by the sage Sārasvata (?) (सारस्-वतीं गतिं चैव लभते नात्र संशयः) 3. 81. 163-164.
दर्दुर: Dardura m.: Name of a mountain. Described as great mountain (महागिरि); Hanūmant and others who accompanied him saw Dardura (along with Sahya and Malaya) near the (southern) ocean (लवणाम्भसः । समीपे) when they came out of the cave 3. 266. 42; mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2.
दर्वीसङ्क्रमण: Darvīsaṅkramaṇa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as famous in the three worlds (त्रैलोक्यविश्रुत); by visiting it (प्राप्य) one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and goes to heaven 3. 82. 40.
दशगङ्गा: Daśagaṅgā f.: Name of a river. The river is mentioned among those holy places by visiting which the high souled persons, who have observed vows, go to the Goloka (? गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44), after they assume heavenly form, wear heavenly garlands, become auspicious and are rich in holy fragrance 13. 105. 46, 48 (for citation see Karatoyinī).
दशाश्वमेधिक: Daśāśvamedhika1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Śālūkinī तीर्थ; by bathing there a pilgrim (तीर्थसेवी) gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 81. 11.
Daśāśvamedhika2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। In Śītavana (?) 3. 81. 48; by bathing there one acquires the highest condition (after death) (गच्छेत परमां गतिम्) 3. 81. 52.

Daśāśvamedhika3 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। On the Gaṅgā (गङ्गायां), near the Haṃsaprapatana तीर्थ 3. 83. 82; the places on the bank of the Gaṅgā are meant for practising austerities; they are the Siddha-kṣetras (यत्र गङ्गा महाराज स देशस् तत् तपोवनम् । सिद्धक्षेत्रं तु तज् ज्ञेयं गङ्गातीरसमाश्रितम् ॥ ) 3. 83. 83.
दासी: Dāsī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 30, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
दिवौकसां: Divaukasāṃ puṣkariṇī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting this तीर्थ a pure person (शुचिः) does not experience bad condition (after death) (न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नोति) and gets the reward of a Vājapeya sacrifice 3. 82. 102.
दिश्: Diś f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 18, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
दीर्घसत्र: Dīrghasatra nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Brahman and other gods, as well as the Siddhas and the great sages who have observed vows perform there long sacrificial sessions and give दक्षिणास् (दीर्घसत्रम् उपासन्ते दक्षिणाभिर् यतव्रताः); just by visiting the तीर्थ (गमनाद् एव) one obtains the fruit of a Rājasūya and an Aśvamedha sacrifice 3. 80. 116-117.
दुर्गशैल: Durgaśaila m.: Name of a mountain. Listed by Saṃjaya as the sixth of the seven mountains of the Śākadvīpa; described as rising high (महोदय) 6. 12. 21, 12-13; the extent in योजनस् of these mountains doubles as one moves from one to the other (तेषां योजनविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रवि-भागशः) 6. 12. 22.
दुर्गा: Durgā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya त्wइचे among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 29 (दुऋगाम् अन्तःशिलां चैव) and 32 (दुर्गाम् अपि च भारत) 6. 10. 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
दृमि: Dṛmi(n) nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as famous in all the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्); famous (दृमीति नाम्ना विख्यातम्) 3. 80. 88, and one that relieves from all sins (सर्व-पापप्रमोचनम्) 3. 80. 88; Brahman and other gods wait there upon Maheśvara 3. 80. 89; by bathing there and by worshipping Rudra, surrounded by hosts of gods, one drives away sins committed since birth (जन्म-प्रभृति पापानि कृतानि नुदते नरः) 3. 80. 89. [See Dṛmī]
दृमी: Dṛmī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as praised by all gods (दृमी चात्र नरश्रेष्ठ सर्वदेवैर् अभिष्टुता) 3. 80. 90; by bathing there one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice 3. 80. 90; Viṣṇu formerly killed the demons and purified himself at this तीर्थ (जित्वा … विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । पुरा शौचं कृतं राजन् हत्वा दैवत-कण्तकान्) 3. 80. 91 (identical with Dṛmi-(n) ?).
दृषद्वती: Dṛṣadvatī f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 14, 13; situated in the north (उदीच्यां … दिशि) 3. 88. 1, 10; Kurukṣetra lay to the north of the Dṛṣadvatī and to the south of the Sarasvatī (दक्षिणेन सरस्वत्या उत्तरेण दृषद्वतीम् । ये वसन्ति कुरुक्षेत्रे) 3. 81. 175. B. Description: Famous (ख्याता) and most holy (पुण्यतमा) 3. 88. 10; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Holy: (1) By bathing in the Dṛṣadvatī and by satis-fying (तर्पयित्वा) gods one secures for himself the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and an Atirātra 3. 81. 73; (2) One who bathes in the confluence of the Dṛṣadvatī and the Kauśikī and who lives on limited food (नियताहारः) is freed of all sins 3. 81. 80; (3) Those who visit, among other holy places, Dṛṣadvatī obtain heavenly form, wear heavenly garlands, become auspicious and, rich in holy fragrance, they go to the Goloka (? गवां विमाने) 13. 105. 47-48, 44 (for citation see Karatoyinī); (4) One should visit the Sarasvatī and the Dṛṣadvatī and, moving along their banks (सरस्वतीदृषद्-वत्यौ सेवमानो ऽनुसंचरेः) and reciting regularly the Vedic text, should bathe at all places (स्वाध्यायशीलः स्थानेषु सर्वेषु समुपस्पृशेः) 12. 148. 12. D. Events: (1) Epic: (i) Śaṃbhu (Śiva) once instru-cted Yudhiṣṭhira on this river (अनुशिष्टो ऽसि  … दृषद्वत्यां च शंभुना) 2. 69. 13; (ii) The Pāṇḍavas, at the start of their forest life, lived on the Sarasvatī, the Dṛṣadvatī and the Yamunā and then went westwards from forest to forest (ययुर् वनेनैव वनं सत-तं पश्चिमां दिशम्) 3. 6. 2; (iii) After Yudhiṣṭhira had received his first instruction in the राजधर्म (12. 56. 11), he and others took bath in the Dṛṣadvatī and, after duly performing the evening rites, entered Hāstinapura 12. 58. 30; (2) Past: It was at Dṛṣadvatī that Vaivarṇya and Varṇa constantly offered holy sacrifices (यजन्तौ क्रतुभिर् नित्यं पुण्यैः) 3. 88. 10-11. E. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 17, 2.
देवकूट: Devakūṭa m.: Name of a तीर्थ (?), of a mountain (?). Frequented by hosts of Brahmanical sages (ब्रह्मर्षिगणसेवित); by visiting it one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and rescues one's family 3. 82. 122.
देवतीर्थ: Devatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing in the Devatīrtha one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 81. 86; it is supposed to be present also at the back of the little finger (कनिष्ठिकायाः पश्चात् तु देवतीर्थम् इहोच्यते) 13. 107. 96.
देवदारुवन: Devadāruvana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who bathes at this तीर्थ, fasts for seven nights, offers water libations to the dead (कृतोदकः) washes off his sins, becomes pure and goes to the world of the gods 13. 26. 25.
देवनद: Devanada m.: Name of a river ? Perhaps not the name of an independent river but the river Sindhu is so characterized (सिन्धुर् देवनदस् तथा); present in bodily form (देहवन्तः) in the Sabhā of Varuṇa 2. 9. 19, 21. [See Sindhu]
देवनदी: Devanadī1 f.: Name of a river. Described as holy (पुण्या); finds men-tion in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 24, 2. [see Devanadī2]

Devanadī2 f.: Various rivers so called. (1) Gaṅgā 1. 158. 20; 3. 108. 2; 3. 155. 85 (महागङ्गा); (2) Ākāśagaṅgā 18. 3. 26, 37, 39 (simply Gaṅgā); (3) Narmadā 13. 2. 18; (4) Kauśikī 3. 110. 1. [See Devanadī1]
देवपथ: Devapatha m.: Name of a तीर्थ (?) By visiting Devapatha one who is restrained and lives on limited food (नियतो नियताशनः) gets the merit (पुण्य) of performing a long festival in honour of gods (? देवसत्रस्य यत् पुण्यं तद् अवाप्नोति मानवः) 3. 83. 42.
देवपर्वत: Devaparvata m.: Name of a mountain. By visiting Devaparvata one is cleansed of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa (ब्रह्म-हत्या विशुध्यति) 13. 26. 40 (= Devagiri: between Ujjain and Mandasor (Aravali Hills ?); see note on the st., Cr. Ed. 17. 1067).
देववन: Devavana nt.: Name of a sacred forest. Situated in the east 3. 85. 3; on the mountain Kuṇḍoda (?) 3. 85. 20; described as pleasing (रम्य) and adorned by ascetics (तापसैर् उपशोभितम्) 3. 85. 21.
देवसभ: Devasabha m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the south (दक्षिणस्याम्) 3. 86. 1; near the sacred place Gokarṇa 3. 86. 12; on this mountain is located the hermi-tage of Tṛṇasomāgni, the pupil of Agastya 3. 86. 14.
देवह्रद: Devahrada1 m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the Śrīparvata 3. 83. 16; by bathing there, one who is pure and has controlled his mind (शुचिः प्रयतमानसः) gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and achieves highest perfection (परां सिद्धिं च गच्छति) 3. 83. 18.

Devahrada2 m.: Name of a तीर्थ, also called Sarvadevahrada (3. 83. 36). Formed in the waters of the river Kṛṣṇaveṇṇā (कृष्णवेण्णाजलोद्भवे); des-cribed as pleasing (रम्य) 3. 83. 34; by just visiting it (गमनाद् एव) one gets the fruit of a hundred Agniṣṭoma sacrifices 3. 83. 35; by bathing at the Sarvadevahrada-tīrtha one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 83. 36.
Devahrada3 m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the mountain Kālaṃjara; by bathing at the Devahrada one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 83. 53.
Devahrada4 m.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing (उपस्पृश्य) there a pilgrim becomes one with Brahman (ब्रह्मभूतो विराजते) 13. 26. 41; (on the river Gaṇḍakī, see note on the st., Cr. Ed. 17. 1067).
देवारण्य: Devāraṇya nt. (pl.): Certain forests, some of them on the mountain Himavant, so designated. Described as holy (पुण्य) 1. 143. 25; many epic and mythological events associated with them: (1) Hiḍimbā sported with Bhīma in many places, some of these being the forests of gods (देवारण्येषु पुण्येषु) 1. 143, 25; (2) Some of the places visited by Ambā for bathing while practising severe austerities were the forests of gods (व्यचरत् काशिकन्या … देवारण्येषु चैव ह … आप्ला-वयत गात्राणि तीव्रम् आस्थाय वै तपः) 5. 187. 24, 26, 28; (3) In order to show Indra to Indrāṇī, Upaśruti took her to a lake after crossing the forests sacred to gods, mountains and the Himavant (देवारण्यान्य् अतिक्रम्य … हिमवन्तम् अतिक्रम्य उत्तरं पार्श्वम् आगमत्) 5. 14. 5; (4) A croco-dile, when delivered from her present condition, told Arjuna that she was an Apsaras, Vargā by name and a favourite of Kubera, who sported in the forests of the gods (अप्सरास्मि महाबाहो देवारण्यविचारिणी । इष्टा धन-पतेर् नित्यं वर्गा नाम) 1. 208. 14.
देविका: Devikā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 15, 13. B. Description: Holy (पुण्या) and frequented by divine sages (देवर्षिसेविता) 3. 80. 115; famous in the worlds (लोकविश्रुता) 3. 80. 110; one of the rivers which are described as best rivers (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठाः), most holy (पुण्यतमाः) and auspicious (शिवाः) 13. 134. 22; all rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Extent: Half a योजन wide and five योजनस् long (अर्ध-योजनविस्तारां पञ्चयोजनम् आयताम् । एतावद् देविकाम् आहुः) 3. 80. 115. D. Holy: Sacred to Triśūlapāṇi (Śiva) 3. 80. 111; by bathing in this river, by worshipping Maheśvara, and by offering a चरु according to one's mite one gets the fruit of a sacrifice which fulfils all wishes (यथाशक्ति चरुं तत्र निवेद्य भरतर्षभ । सर्वकाम-समृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य लभते फलम् ॥ ) 3. 80. 112; one who bathes in Devikā is awakened in a Vimāna while being praised by the Apsarases (विबोध्यते विमानस्थः सो ऽप्सरोभिर् अभिष्टुतः) 13. 26. 9; one of the rivers which are supposed to have waters of all the तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युताः) 13. 134. 12; also one of the rivers which are called mothers of the fire-hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्र-कीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 21, 24 (for Nī.'s remark see Kapilā); there are many sacred places on it like Kāma, Yajana, Yājana, Brahma-vālukā and Puṣpanyāsa 3. 80. 113-114. E. Importance: (1) Descendants in the family of the Brāhmaṇas who hail from the Devikā are famous (प्रसूतिर् यत्र वि-प्राणां श्रूयते भरतर्षभ) 3. 80. 110; (2) Devikā is one of the rivers who wait on Śiva for his bath (उपस्पर्शनहेतोस् त्वा समीपस्था उपासते) 13. 134. 12; these rivers were conversant with the duties of women (स्त्रीधर्मकुशलाः) and hence were consulted and honoured by Umā before she expounded स्त्रीधर्म to Śiva 13. 134. 19-20, 14, 25; (3) Finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 14 and in the Tīrthavaṃśa 13. 26. 3, 9.
देव्यास्: Devyās tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ (?) Situated on the confluence of Sarasvatī and Aruṇā; described as world famous (लोक-विश्रुत) 3. 81. 131; a pilgrim should visit it after visiting the Madhusravatīrtha 3. 81. 130-131; by fasting there for three nights and by bathing, one is freed of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa, obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and an Atirātra, and purifies his family up to seven generations (आसप्तमं कुलं चैव पुनाति भरतर्षभ) 3. 81. 132.
द्युतिमत्: Dyutimant m.: Name of a mountain. Name of the second among the six mountains of the Kuśadvīpa; it is made of gold (द्वितीयो हेमपर्वतः । द्युतिमान् नाम) 6. 13. 9-10; all the six mountains are described as the best mountains (पर्व-तोत्तमाः) 6. 13. 11; the distance between them doubles as one moves from the one to the other (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 13. 11.
द्युतिमन्त्: Dyutimant m.: Name of a mountain. Name of the second among the six mountains of the Kuśadvīpa; it is made of gold (द्वितीयो हेमपर्वतः । द्युतिमान् नाम) 6. 13. 9-10; all the six mountains are described as the best mountains (पर्व-तोत्तमाः) 6. 13. 11; the distance between them doubles as one moves from the one to the other (तेषाम् अन्तरविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 13. 11.
द्रोणशर्मपद: Droṇaśarmapada nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who bathes there is waited upon by the hosts of Apsarases (सेव्यते सो ऽप्सरो-गनैः) 13. 26. 26.
द्वैतवन: Dvaitavana1 nt.: Name of a lake (situated in the forest of the same name). A. Location: Situated near the river Sarasvatī (सरस्वतीम् एत्य निवासकामाः सरस् ततो द्वैतवनं प्रतीयुः) 3. 174. 21. B. Descriprion: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 25. 12, 13; 3. 27. 2; 3. 229. 13; suitable for holy people (पुण्यजनोचित) 3. 25. 10; famous (विख्यात) 3. 25. 12; beautiful (रम्य) 3. 25. 10; having many fruits and flowers (बहुपुष्पफल) 3. 25. 10; large (महत्) 3. 25. 12; resorted to by different kinds of birds (नानाद्विजनिषेवित) 3. 25. 10. C. Epic events related to the lake: (1) Arjuna recommended to Yudhiṣṭhira a place near the Dvaitavana lake for their residence during the period of their forest life; Yudhiṣṭhira agreed to this suggestion and the Pāṇḍavas proceeded towards the lake (इदं द्वैतवनं नाम सरः … । अत्रेमा द्वादश समा विहरेमेति रोचये) । यदि ते ऽनुमतं राजन् … । ममाप्य् एतन् मतं पार्थ त्वया यत् समुदाहृतम्) 3. 25. 10-13; (2) when the Pāṇḍavas lived in the Dvaitavana forest, the lake Dvaitavana, due to the sound of the recitation of the Vedas heard all around, looked like the world of Brahman (ब्रह्मलोकसमं पुण्यम् आसीद् द्वैतवनं सरः) 3. 27. 2; (3) While returning from the Gandhamādana along with Arjuna, the Pāṇḍavas reached Sarasvatī and then went to the Dvaitavana lake with a view to settling down there (सरस्वतीम् एत्य निवासकामाः सरस् ततो द्वैतवनं प्रतीयुः) 3. 174. 21; (4) Karṇa advised Duryodhana to show his pomp to the Pāṇḍavas who were reported to be residing near the Dvaitavana lake 3. 226. 12-13; (5) When permitted by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Duryodhana, Karṇa and others started for the Dvaitavana lake and settled down at a distance of just a गव्यूति (= 2 क्रोशस्) from the lake (गव्यूतिमात्रे न्यवसद् राजा दुर्योधनस् तदा) 3. 228. 25, 29; (6) Duryodhana, once out for hunting, went near the Dvaitavana lake; he asked his servants to set up sporting tents (आक्रीडावसथाः क्षिप्रं क्रियन्ताम्); so they started towards the lake but the Gandharvas who had arrived there before, obstructed Duryodhana's servants who were approaching the lake; when this was reported to Duryodhana he asked his army to oust the Gandharvas; so they returned to the lake 3. 229. 13, 16-19, 23; (7) The return of the Pāṇḍavas to the Dvaitavana lake after their encounter with the Gandharvas is referred to in the list of the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan (घोषयात्रा च गन्धर्-वैर् यत्र युद्धं किरीटिनः ॥ पुनर् आगमनं चैव तेषां द्वैतवनं सरः) 1. 2. 122-123; (8) When Balarāma visited the Dvaitavana forest he bathed in the Dvaitavana lake (not named) and after worshipping the Brāhmaṇas gave them many articles of enjoyment (आप्लुत्य सलिले चापि  … तथैव दत्त्वा विप्रेभ्यः परिभोगान् सुपुष्कलान्) 9. 36. 27-28.

Dvaitavana2 nt.: Name of a forest. A. Location: Situated along the river Bhogavatī (= Sarasvatī) (मनोरमां भोगवतीम् उपेत्य) 3. 25. 20; (तत् काननं प्राप्य … विजह्रुः … सरस्वती-शालवनेषु तेषु) 3. 26. 1; 3. 174. 23-24; Balarāma arrived at the Dvaitavana and then proceeded along the southern bank of the Sarasvatī (ततः प्रायाद् बलो राजन् दक्षिणेन सरस्वतीम्) 9. 36. 24, 28. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 25. 16; 3. 27. 7; 3. 294. 43; 9. 36. 26; pleasing (रम्य) 3. 25. 16; 3. 295. 3; large (महा-वन) 3. 25. 17; 3. 26. 3; 3. 242. 7; (महारण्य) 3. 27. 1; abode of religious persons (वने धर्मभृतां निवासे) 3. 25. 20; full of many beasts of prey and deer (बहुव्यालमृगाकीऋण) 3. 243. 21; the forest is also described in 3. 25. 17-20 (having many kinds of trees and birds, which are designated, elephants and hosts of perfected sages). C. Epic events: (1) After killing the demon Kirmīra in the Kāmyaka forest, the Pāṇḍavas proceeded towards the Dvaita-vana 3. 12. 18; (2) The Pāṇḍavas wishing to settle down for their forest life near the lake Dvaitavana, entered the forest Dvaitavana 3. 25. 13, 16; (3) In the Dvaitavana (not named) the Pāṇḍavas sported in the auspici-ous woods of the Śāla trees along the river Sarasvatī; there Yudhiṣṭhira satisfied the twice-borns by offering them large-sized roots and fruit; there Dhaumya officiated for their religious rites to gods and manes; sage Mārkaṇḍeya arrived there as a guest of the Pāṇḍavas 3. 26. 1-4; (4) When the Pāṇḍa-vas lived in the Dvaitavana, the forest was full of Brāhmaṇas; the forest resounded with the sound of Vedic recitations of the Brāhmaṇas and the sound of the bow-strings of the Pāṇḍavas; thus the Kṣatriya valour, united with Brahmanic lustre, shone all the more in the forest (संसृष्टं ब्रह्मणा क्षत्रं भूय एव व्यरोचत); Baka Dāl-bhya pointed out to Yudhiṣṭhira Bhṛgus and others who, when protected by Yudhiṣṭhira, gave offerings in fire (चरन्ति धर्मं पुण्ये ऽस्मिंस् त्वया गुप्ता धृतव्रताः) 3. 27. 1-8; (5) Vyāsa advised Yudhiṣṭhira to leave the Dvaitavana since staying long at one place was not desirable; hence he went from the Dvaita to the Kāmyaka forest 3. 37. 31-32, 37; (6) Later when the Pāṇḍavas returned to the Dvaitavana from the Gandhamādana, the ascetics in the forest returned to them 3. 174. 22; (7) Karṇa suggested to Duryodhana to visit the lake Dvaitavana to show the pomp of the Kauravas to the Pāṇḍavas 3. 226. 12-13; Duryodhana approved of this idea; his only purpose was to oust the Pāṇḍavas from the forest (न हि द्वैतवने किंचिद् विद्यते ऽन्यत् प्रयो-जनम् । उत्सादनम् ऋते तेषाम् वनस्थानां मम द्विषः), and to show them, who were in miserable condition, his pomp 3. 227. 5, 8-11; Karṇa suggested that their pretext to visit the Dvaitavana should be to meet the cowherds who awaited Duryodhana's visit (घोषा द्वैतवने सर्वे त्वत्प्रतीक्षा नराधिप । घोषयात्रापदेशेन गमिष्यामो न संशयः) 3. 227. 19, 23; (8) Yudhiṣṭhira reminded the Kauravas through Saṃjaya of their defeat at the hands of the Gandharvas in the Dvaitavana, where they had arrived for the Ghoṣayātrā, and their subsequent release from the captivity of their adversaries by Bhīmasena and Arjuna 5. 23. 25; Śalya later alleged that in that encounter with the Gandharvas Karṇa was the first to run away from the battle 8. 28. 59; (9) After the Ghoṣayātrā incident the Pāṇḍavas lived happily in the Dvaitavana forest 3. 235. 25; (10) Duḥśāsana sent a messenger to the Pāṇḍavas and the Brāhmaṇas living in the Dvaitavana to invite them to attend Duryodhana's Vaiṣṇava Yajña 3. 242. 7; (11) Yudhi-ṣṭhira, disturbed by Karṇa's vow to kill Arjuna, thought of leaving the Dvaita-vana 3. 243. 21; (12) While living in the Dvaitavana, Yudhiṣṭhira once saw deer in a dream who requested him to leave the forest and go elsewhere as, on account of their pre-sence, only a few deer were left in that forest 3. 244. 2, 5; (13) At the end of the twelfth year of their forest life the Pāṇḍavas went from the Kāmyaka to the Mārkaṇḍeyā-śrama in the Dvaitavana 3. 294. 43; 3. 295. 3; (14) During their stay in the Dvaita-vana the Pāṇḍavas, while once braving for the sake of a Brāhmaṇa (ब्राह्मणार्थे परा-क्रान्ताः), met with great difficulty which, however, ended happily 17. 3. 18-19; 18. 3. 31 (a reference to the Yakṣapraśṇa episode; Yudhiṣṭhira was tested by Dharma in that episode which took place in the Dvaitavana 3. 295. 7-3. 298. 25); (15) Yudhiṣṭhira, at the end of the twelfth year, while dismiss-ing those who stayed with him in the forest, asked them to tell people that they did not know where the Pāṇḍavas went after they (the Pāṇḍavas) left them in the Dvaitavana 4. 4. 5; (16) In the Dvaitavana Arjuna used to praise the heroic qualities of Sātyaki for Yudhiṣṭhira 7. 85. 61; (17) Yudhiṣṭhira, humiliated by Karṇa, blamed Arjuna for not killing Karṇa and told Arjuna that he should have admitted to the Pāṇḍavas in the Dvaitavana itself that he would not be able to stand up to Karṇa in the war 8. 48. 2; (18) Yudhiṣṭhira was dejected at the thought of the destruction in the war and was think-ing of retiring to forest; Draupadī then reminded him of his resolve to kill Duryodhana and rule the earth which he had announced to his brothers in the Dvaitavana 12. 14. 8; (19) In the Dvaitavana, Balarāma met the sages, bathed in Dvaitavana lake (not named) and then proceeded along the southern bank of the Sarasvatī 9. 36. 26-28.
द्वैपायन: Dvaipāyana m.: Name of a lake (ह्रद, जलाशय). A. Description: Famous (ख्यात) 9. 29. 53; pleasing (हृद्य), having cool and dirt-free water (शीतामलजल), looking like another ocean (द्वितीयम् इव सागरम्) 9. 29. 54. B. Epic event: After the fall of Ulūka and Śakuni, Duryodhana left the battlefield and ran to the lake; he entered it controlling its water with his special powers, and remain-ed there concealed (lake not named) 9. 28. 23, 25, 49, 51-53, 57-58; (तं ह्रदं प्राविशच् चापि विष्टभ्यापः स्वमायया) 9. 29. 7, 43, 54, 61, 64; 9. 30. 2-4 9. 31. 36; Kṛpa, Aśvatthāman and Kṛtavarman, when informed by Saṃjaya about the whereabouts of Duryodhana, proceeded towards the lake Dvaipāyana (not named) 9. 29. 4, 9-10; Duryodhana's hiding himself in the lake was accidentally known by the hunters of Bhīma 9. 29. 30; when they reported it to Bhīma, the Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa, and all the Kṣatriyas rushed to the lake Dvaipāyana 9. 29. 45, 47, 53, 57; 9. 30. 1-2; Yudhiṣṭhira challenged Duryodhana who hid in the lake (not named) to save his life to come out and fight with the Pāṇḍavas 9. 30. 17 (जलाशय), 24, 32 (जलाशय); Duryodhana's entering the lake Dvaipāyana, the Pāṇḍavas' forcing him out of the tamed waters (स्तम्भिते सलिले), and Duryodhana's getting out of the lake with his गदा reported later by Nārada to Balarāma 9. 53. 27-29; according to Vāsudeva's report of the war to his father Vasudeva, Bhīmasena, who ran after Duryodhana fleeing from the battlefield, saw him in the water of the lake Dvaipā-yana; the five Pāṇḍavas sat near the lake and forced him out by using sharp words 14. 59. 27-29.
दधीचाश्रम: Dadhīcāśrama m.: An आश्रम of Dadhīca. A. Location: On the other bank of Sarasvatī (सरस्वत्याः परे पारे) 3. 98. 13. B. Description: Very attractive (सुमनो-रम) 3. 98. 17; beautified at various places (तेषु तेष्व् अवकाशेषु शोभितम्) 3. 98. 17; having splendour like that of heaven (त्रि-विष्टपसमप्रख्य) 3. 98. 17; covered with different kinds of trees and creepers (नाना-द्रुमलतावृत) 3. 98. 13; humming with the sounds produced by the bees, mixed with the notes of the male cuckoo, and alive with the sounds of Jīvakas (जीवं जीवक-नादितम्) 3. 98. 13; buffalos, boars, Sṛma-ras and Camara deer moved everywhere freely without fear of tigers (तत्र तत्रानु-चरितं शार्दूलभयवर्जितैः) 3. 98. 14; resounding all around with the trumpets of elephants in rut sporting with female elephants in lakes (करेणुभिर् वारणैश् च प्रभिन्नकरटामुखैः । सरोवगाढैः क्रीडद्भिः समन्ताद् अनुनादितम् ॥ ) 3. 98. 15; resounding with the loud roars of lions and tigers and of other animals lying con-cealed in caves (अपरैश् चापि संलीनैर् गुहाकन्दरवासिभिः) 3. 98. 16. C. Past event: Gods, led by Nārāyaṇa, went to the आश्रम of Dadhīca to ask for his bones (दधीचस्याश्रमं ययुः) 3. 98. 12; (दधीचाश्रमम् आगमन्) 3. 98. 17; there they saw Dadhīca shining like the sun 3. 98. 18.
दन्तकूर: Dantakūra nt.: Name of a city. (1) Sahadeva defeated the assembled kings of the southern countries at Danta-kūra (यो दन्तकूरे व्यजयन् नृदेवान् समा-गतान् दाक्षिणात्यान् महीपान्) 3. 119. 18; (2) Sahadeva defeated the assembled Kaliṅgas at Dantakūra (सहदेवः कलिङ्-गान् समागतान् अजयद् दन्तकूरे) 5. 23. 23 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 5. 23. 24; दन्तकूरः सङ्ग्रामः तस्मिन्); (3) Kṛṣṇa crushed the Kaliṅgas at Dantakūra 5. 47. 70 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 48. 76; दन्तकूरे सङ्ग्रामे; but he also mentions the view of other commentators according to whom Dantakūra was the name of a city (नगर).
दिलीपस्य: Dilīpasya āśramaḥ m.: An आश्रम established by Dilīpa. Ambā, while practising austerities in order to be able to kill Bhīṣma, visited many holy places, one of them being the आश्रम of Dilīpa (दिलीपस्याश्रमे तथा) 5. 187. 27; she bathed at these holy places and practised severe austerities (एतेषु तीर्थेषु तदा काशिकन्या … आप्लावयत गात्राणि तीव्रम् आस्थाय वै तपः) 5. 187. 28.
दिवःप्रस्थ: Divaḥprastha nt.: Name of a town. It was a big town of Senābindu (सेना-बिन्दोः पुरं महत्) 2. 24. 12; Arjuna, in his expedition to the north (प्रययाव् उत्तरां तस्माद् दिशम् 2. 24. 1) before the Rājasūya, encamped there with his army and from there he attacked the Paurava king Viṣvagaśva 2. 24. 12-13.
दर्जया: Darjayā f.: Name of a city. The आश्रम of Agastya was located near it; Yudhiṣṭhira, having reached the आश्रम, lived there; he asked Lomaśa why Vātāpi was put out of action there (अगस्-त्याश्रमम् आसाद्य दुर्जयायाम् उवास ह । … अगस्त्येनेह वातापिः किमर्थम् उपशामि-तः) 3. 94. 1-2 (Nī. on 3. 96. 1 takes दुर्-जया as an epithet ‘invincible’ of the city of Vātāpi, called Maṇimatī: दुर्जयायां वातापिपुर्यां मणिमती संज्ञायां).
द्वारका: Dvārakā, Dvāravatī f.: Name of a city, also called Kuśasthalī (2. 13. 49; 12. 326. 83, 85), Ānartanagarī (5. 7. 4; 14. 51. 41), Ānartanagara (3. 21. 1), Ānartapurī (14. 51. 56), Vṛṣṇipura (3. 21. 4; 3. 180. 25). A. Location: In the west (प्रतीचीं दिशम् आश्रिताः) 2. 13. 49; (समावृत्ताः पश्चि-मां दिशम् एव ते । ददृशुर् द्वारकां चापि) 17. 1. 43; in the Anarta country (आनर्तम् एवाभिमुखाः … वृष्णिपुरं प्रविश्य) 3. 180. 25; in the Surāṣṭra country (सुराष्ट्रेषु  … पुण्या द्वारवती तत्र) 3. 86. 20-21; near the Raivataka mountain (रईवतेनोपशोभि-ताम्) 2. 13. 49; 2. 13. 52; 14. 58. 3-4. B. Description: Holy (पुण्या) 3. 13. 31; pleasing (रम्या) 2. 13. 49; 5. 7. 4; 14. 58. 3; 14. 84. 13; liked by the sages (ऋषिकान्ता) 3. 13, 41; offering different kinds of enjoy-ments (भोगवती) 3. 13. 31; full of jewels (रत्नसंपूर्णा) 16. 8. 40; adorned by Raivataka mountain (रैवतेनोपशोभिताम्) 2. 13. 49; guarded by Vṛṣṇi heroes (वृष्णि-वीराभिरक्षिता) 14. 84. 13; the place of residence of the Vṛṣṇis (वृष्णिनिलय) 16. 6. 4; having ramparts and watch towers (प्राकाराट्टालकोपेता) 16. 7. 17; referred to chiefly as पूरी 1. 212. 9; 1. 213. 55; 2. 13. 49, 65; 2. 42. 49, 55; 3. 16. 2, 4; 3. 21. 9; 5. 7. 3; 12. 326. 83, 84; 14. 15. 21, 26; 14. 51. 42; 14. 58. 3; 14. 84. 15; 16. 5. 7; 16. 7. 13; but also as नगर 3. 16. 12; 3. 21. 8; 16. 2. 17, 18; 16. 8. 10; नगरी 16. 7. 17; and पुर 3. 16. 18. C. Forti-fication: The Yādavas fortified Dvārakā in such a way that even gods could not reach it and women could defend it (तथैव दुर्गसंस्कारं देवैर् अपि दुरा-सदम् ॥ स्त्रियो ऽपि यस्यां युध्येयुः किं पुनर् वृष्णिपुंगवाः) 2. 13. 50-51. D. Epic events: (1) The Yādavas fled to the west from Mathurā due to fear of Jarāsandha and repaired to Kuśasthalī; they settled down there and fortified the town; they lived in Kuśasthalī without fear from any quarter (अकुतोभयाः); seeing the mountain (Raivataka) nearby and the Mādhavītīrtha, the Yādavas were highly delighted 2. 13. 49-52, 65; hence the city is referred to as the residence of the Yāda-vas (यदुसदन) 8. 26. 63; (2) Hearing that Śiśupāla was killed by Kṛṣṇa, Śālva, during the absence of Kṛṣṇa from Dvā-rakā, attacked the city riding in his Saubha town; he killed young Vṛṣṇi heroes who defended the city and destroyed all gardens (पुरोद्यानानि सर्वाणि भेदयाम् आस दुर्म-तिः) 3. 15. 5-7; hearing that Śrautaśrava (Śiśupāla) was killed, Śālva besieged Dvāra-vatī from all sides; he mounted his Saubha, flying in the sky, and from there attacked the city; the fortification and the defence arrangements of the city were looked after by Gada, Sāmba, Uddhava and others according to the rules laid down in the Śāstras (शास्त्रदृष्टेन विधिना संयूक्ता); drinking liquor was forbidden in the town to avoid negligence on the part of citizens (आघोषितं च नगरे न पातव्या सुरेति ह । प्रमादं परिरक्षद्भिः) 3. 16. 2-18; Dvārakā was well guarded by king Āhuka by giving largesses (द्वारका भूरिदक्षिणैः । आहुकेन सुगुप्ता च राज्ञा) 3. 16. 23; Śālva attacked Dvārakā with the speed of the king of birds (अभिसारयाम् आस तदा वेगेन पत-गेन्द्रवत्) 3. 17. 7; all the people in Dvārakā were bewildered when Śālva descended on the earth with his Saubha (सौभस्थं पृथिवीगतम्) 3. 17. 28; when Śālva was defeated by the Vṛṣṇis led by Pradyumna he left Dvārakā mounting his Saubha 3. 20. 27; (3) At the end of the Rājasūya Kṛṣṇa wished to return to Dvārakā 2. 42. 46, 52; Yudhiṣṭhira approved of Kṛṣṇa's return to Dvāravatī 2. 42. 49; when Kṛṣṇa returned to Ānartanagara after the Rāja-sūya of Yudhiṣṭhira at Indraprastha he saw Dvārakā lack-lustre; it was bereft of the sound of Vedic studies and Vedic sacrifices (आनर्तनगरं मुक्तं ततो ऽहम् अगमं तदा । महाक्रतौ राजसूये निवृत्ते … ॥ अपश्यं द्वारकां चाहं महाराज हत-त्विषम् । निःस्वाध्यायवषट्कारम्); noble women of the town did not put on orna-ments; the gardens of Dvārakā were chang-ed beyond recognition (अनभिज्ञेयरूपाणी द्वारकोपवनानी च); Kṛṣṇa found Vṛṣṇi-pura with its men and women very much ill at ease (अस्वस्थनरनारीकम् इदं वृष्णि-पुरं भृशम्); the siege of Dvārakā by Śālva and lifting of the siege later by him was reported to Kṛṣṇa; enraged, he asked the Yādava heroes to be watchful in the city (अप्रमादः सदा कार्यो नगरे याद-वर्षभाः) and left for the destruction of Śālva; he vowed not to return to Dvāravatī without killing Śālva (नाहत्वा तं निवर्-तिष्ये पुरीं द्वारवतीं प्रति) 3. 21. 1-9; he asked Sātyaki, Baladeva, and Pradyumna to protect Dvārakā and his father Vasudeva 3. 22. 16-17; during the fight with Śālva, a certain resident of Dvārakā (पुरुषः कश्चिद् द्वारकानिलयः), a servant (परि-चारकः) of Āhuka, met Kṛṣṇa and gave him a false message from Āhuka; accord-ing to the message Śālva had attacked Dvārakā and killed the son of Śūrasena (Vasudeva); hence Kṛṣṇa was advised to leave the battle, return to Dvārakā and protect it; that should be Kṛṣṇa's prime concern (द्वारकाम् एव रक्षस्व कार्यम् एतन् महत् तव) 3. 22. 12-14; Kṛṣṇa then mentally blamed Sātyaki and others who were entrusted with the protection of Dvā-rakā and of Vasudeva 3. 22. 16-17; (Kṛṣṇa, however, soon realized that he was tricked by Śālva by his माया and started to fight with him again); he was incited to action by his charioteer who reminded him that Dvārakā was ransacked by Śālva (द्वारका चावमर्दिता) 3. 23. 25; (4) Kṛṣṇa told Yudhiṣṭhira that he was not in Dvārakā when the game of dice was played in Hās-tinapura 3. 14. 1; he heard of the द्यूत only when he returned to Dvārakā after vanquishing Śālva 3. 14. 15; (5) After informing Yudhiṣṭhira in the forest about Śālva's attacking Dvārakā and Kṛṣṇa's sub-sequent battle with him, he comforted Yudhi-ṣṭhira and returned to Dvārakā 3. 23. 42-45; (6) Dvārakā was once burnt by Śiśupāla when Kṛṣṇa and others had gone to Prāg-jyotiṣapura 2. 42. 7; (7) Prophecies regard-ing Dvārakā: (i) Nārāyaṇa told Nārada that at the conjunction of Dvāpara and Kali (द्वापरस्य कलेश् चैव संधौ 12. 326. 82) he would be born at Mathurā but would make Kuśasthalī (i. e. Dvārakā) his residence (कुशस्थलीं करिष्यामि निवासं द्वारकां पुरीम्) 12. 326. 83-85; while residing in that city he would kill Naraka, Mura and Pīṭha 12. 326. 84; he would also kill the demons and take the wealth of Prāgjyotiṣapura to Kuśasthalī (प्राग्ज्योतिषपुरं रम्यं नानाधन-समन्वितम् । कुशस्थलीं नयिष्यामि) 12. 326. 85; having lessened the burden of the earth he would bring about the destruction of the Sātvata heroes, his kinsmen and of Dvārakā (कृत्वा भारावतरणं वसु-धाया यथेप्सितम् । सर्वसात्वतमुख्या-नां द्वारकायाश् च सत्तम । करिष्ये प्र-लयं घोरम् आत्मज्ञातिविनाशनम् ॥ ) 12. 326. 92; (ii) prophesied also by Arjuna that Dvārakā, which was made his home by Kṛṣṇa, would be drowned in the sea by him (द्वारकाम् आत्मसात् कृत्वा समुद्रं गमयिष्यसि) 3. 13. 31; (iii) Kṛṣṇa too had foretold that when Arjuna would leave Dvārakā taking with him the citizens, the city, together with its ramparts and watch-towers, would be instantly inundated by the sea (इमां च नगरीं सद्यः प्रतियाते ध-नंजये । प्राकाराट्टालकोपेतां समुद्रः प्लावयिष्यति) 16. 7. 17; 16. 8. 10; (8) Des-truction of Dvārakā: Arjuna advised all people to leave the town at the end of a week and stay outside 16. 8. 12; before leaving Dvārakā, the citizens (द्वारकावासि-नः) attended the funeral of Vasudeva 16. 8. 19-23; when all people had left, the city was overrun by the sea (सागरः … । द्वार-कां रत्नसंपूऋणां जलेनाप्लावयत् तदा ॥ ) 16. 8. 40; the people of Dvārakā witnessed the event the like of which had not happened before (अद्भुतम्) 16. 8. 41; the people of Dvārakā who followed Arjuna to Indra-prastha were handed over to Vajra 16. 8. 73: the Pāṇḍavas when they started on their great final journey (महाप्रस्थान) went, on their way, to the west and saw Dvārakā inundated by the sea (ददृशुर् द्वारकां चापि सागरेण परिप्लुताम्) 17. 1. 43; Arjuna's going to Dvāravatī, bereft of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, and his taking with him the people of Dvāravatī listed in the con-tents of the Mausalaparvan 1. 2. 223, 226; (9) After the Pāṇḍavas were established at Indraprastha Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma left for Dvāravatī with the consent of the Pāṇḍavas 1. 199. 50. (10) During the period of his exile Arjuna went from Raivataka mountain to Dvārakā; the city, even up to the modest houses (?), was decorated to welcome him (अलंकृता द्वारका … अपि निष्कुटकेष्व् अपि) 1. 210. 15-16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 218. 16: निष्कुटेषु गृहारामेष्व् अपि अलंकृता किम् उत राजमार्गादिषु); the people of Dvārakā rushed to the main roads to see Arjuna; women in large numbers rushed to the windows (?) (अवलोकेषु नारीणाम् सहस्राणि शतानि च); there was a great gathering (समवायो महान् अभूत्) of the Bhojas, the Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas; Arjuna lived (in Dvārakā) in the house of Kṛṣṇa for many nights 1. 210. 17-21; once, while Subhadrā was returning to Dvā-rakā after worshipping Raivataka mountain she was kidnapped by Arjuna; the helpless soldiers cried aloud and ran towards Dvā-rakā 1. 212. 7, 9; the incident is referred to in 8. 26. 63; (11) The Yādavas, returned to Dvāravatī after visiting Indraprastha where they had gone to give gifts to the Pāṇḍa-vas in connection with the marriage of Subhadrā 1. 213. 55; Subhadrā's abduction by Arjuna from Dvārakā referred to (i) in the Anukramaṇīparvan 1. 1. 103; also listed in the contents of the Ādiparvan narrated in the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan 1. 2. 92, (ii) in Vaiśaṃpāyana's summary of the Mahā-bhārata events 1. 55. 32-34, and (iii) in the Saṃbhavaparvan of the Ādiparvan 1. 90. 85; (12) After asking Maya to build a सभा for the Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa left for Dvārakā 2. 2. 23; (13) Yudhiṣṭhira sent a messenger to Dvārakā to invite Kṛṣṇa, living in Dvārakā, for consultations regard-ing the Rājasūya 2. 12. 29; at the end of the Rājasūya, Yudhiṣṭhira consented to Kṛṣṇa's return to Dvāravatī; accordingly Kṛṣṇa reached Dvāravatī 2. 42. 49, 55, 60; (14) The sons of Draupadī, during the period of exile of the Pāṇḍavas, went to Vṛṣṇipura situated in the Ānarta country 3. 180. 25; later, Satyabhāmā informed Draupadī that her sons were all well and happy at Dvāra-vatī 3. 224. 11; (15) Before going to the Virāṭanagara for the अज्ञातवास, Yudhi-ṣṭhira sent away Indrasena and others, with their chariots, to Dvāravatī 4. 4. 3; the spies, who were sent by Duryodhana in search of the Pāṇḍavas, told him that the charioteers of the Pāṇḍavas had reached Dvāravatī but neither the Pāṇḍavas nor Kṛṣṇā was to be found in Dvāravatī 4. 24. 15-16; (11) After the marriage of Abhi-manyu, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and others, per-mitted by Virāṭa, went to Dvārakā; after Kṛṣṇa's departure to Dvārakā, Yudhiṣṭhira started making all kinds of preparations for the war (चक्रुः साङ्ग्रामिकं सर्वम्) 5. 5. 11-12; 5. 7. 1 (Dvāravatī); (12) When Duryodhana knew through his messe-ngers and spies that Kṛṣṇa had returned to Dvārakā, he started to go there to seek Kṛṣṇa's help in war; that very day Arjuna too arrived in Ānartanagarī; both of them, after reaching Dvārakā, saw Kṛṣṇa sleep-ing 5. 7. 3 (आनर्तनगरीं रम्यां जगा-माशु धनंजयः) 5. 7. 4, 5; (13) When Balarāma started for his pilgrimage he, on his way, asked his servants to bring from Dvārakā all the materials and utensils required for the pilgrimage, as also the sacred fires and priests (संभारांस् तीर्थ-यात्रायां सर्वोपकरणानि च । आनयध्वं द्वारकाया अग्नीन् वै याजकांस् तथा) 9. 34. 15; when Balarāma chose to go to the battlefield to watch the duel between Bhīma and Duryodhana, he sent away his co-pilgrims and attendants to Dvārakā 9. 53. 32; at the end of the duel, Balarāma, expressing his disapproval of the way Bhīma brought about the downfall of Duryodhana, left for Dvārakā 9. 59. 26; when he left for Dvāravatī, the Pāñcālas and the Pāṇḍavas, did not feel very happy 9. 59. 27; (14) When the sacrificial horse for the Aśvamedha of Yudhiṣṭhira reached Dvāravatī, king Ugrasena came out of the town to honour Arjuna who accompanied the horse 14. 84. 13-15; when Yudhiṣṭhira asked Kṛṣṇa to give some news about Arjuna (who was accompanying the horse), Kṛṣṇa told him that a confidential attendant who lived in Dvārakā (द्वारकावासी ममा-प्तः पुरुषः) had seen him (Arjuna) who, fighting many battles, was emaciated (बहु-संग्रामकर्शितम्) 14. 88. 9; (15) After the war, Kṛṣṇa informed Arjuna his intention to return to Dvāravatī to meet his father, Baladeva and others, if permitted by Yudhi-ṣṭhira, but not otherwise; hence he wanted Yudhiṣṭhira to be informed by Arjuna about his wish to go to Dvārakā 14. 15. 20-21, 26, 31; before Kṛṣṇa's return to Dvārakā, Arjuna wanted Kṛṣṇa to tell him once again what he taught him before in the Gītā 14. 16. 6-7; Arjuna approved Kṛṣṇa's wish to return to Dvārakā; so he suggest-ed that they should go to Hāstinapura to seek Yudhiṣṭhira's permission for Kṛṣṇa's return to Dvārakā 14. 50. 51; 14. 51. 23; Arjuna sought Yudhiṣṭhira's permission for Kṛṣṇa's return to Ānartanagarī 14. 51. 40-41; Yudhiṣṭhira gave Kṛṣṇa his permi-ssion to return to Dvāravatī to see his father 14. 51. 42; Arjuna and others emb-raced Kṛṣṇa when he left Hāstinapura to go to Dvārakā 14. 52. 1; (16) Yudhiṣṭhira was grieved to think of what Subhadrā, who was then in Dvārakā (द्वारकावासिनी), would say to Kṛṣṇa when he returned to Dvārakā (since her son was killed in war) 12. 1. 16; (17) Aśvatthāman once went to Dvārakā where he stayed for some time honoured by the Vṛṣṇis; he wanted to exchange his Brahmaśiras missile for the Sudarśana of Kṛṣṇa; while he was in Dvāravatī (वसन् द्वारवतीम् अनु), one day he approached Kṛṣṇa who was sitting alone on seashore; Kṛṣṇa informed Aśvatthāman that none of the Vṛṣṇi and the Andhaka heroes who lived in Dvārakā had ever asked him to part with his Sudarśana 10. 12. 11-12, 15, 31-33; (18) The Yādavas, headed by Sāraṇa, once saw Viśvāmitra, Kaṇva, Nārada and other sages who were on a visit to Dvārakā 16. 2. 4; by the proclamation of a royal decree Āhuka prohibited fermentation of spirituous liquor in all the houses of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas living in the town (Dvārakā) (अद्यप्रभृति सर्वेषु वृष्ण्यन्धकगृहेष्व्-इह । सुरासवो न कर्तव्यः सर्वैर् नगर-वासिभिः) 16. 2. 17-18; one of the bad omens that occurred for the citizens of Dvārakā was that a laughing black woman with white teeth entered the houses at night, stole the marriage threads of women while they were asleep, and ran through the streets of Dvārakā (काली स्त्री पाण्डुरैर् दन्तैः प्रविश्य हसती निशि । स्त्रियः स्व-प्नेषु मुष्णन्ती द्वारकां परिधावति) 16. 4. 1 (Nī. on Bom.
