Ed. 16. 3. 1: मुष्णन्ती स्त्रीणाम् मङ्गलसूत्रादिकं चोरयन्ती); when the Yādavas were destroyed, Kṛṣṇa entered Dvāravatī and told Vasudeva to guard the women folk and wait for the arrival of Arjuna in Dvāravatī 16. 5. 7; 16. 7. 13; when Arjuna reached Dvārakā with Dāruka the city appeared to him like a woman who had lost her husband (मृत-नाथाम् इव स्त्रियम्) 16. 6. 4; Arjuna, after he witnessed the plight of Dvārakā and the women of Kṛṣṇa he wept loudly and fell down on the ground 16. 6. 12. E. Past events or events not related to the epic narrative: (1) Kṛṣṇa told Uttaṅka whom he met on his way to Dvārakā that he (Uttaṅka) should think of him (Kṛṣṇa) if he desired something 14. 54. 13; Govinda (Kṛṣṇa) gave boon to Uttaṅka and went to Dvārakā in the company of Sātyaki 14. 58. 2, 3 (Dvāravatī); (2) Pious king Nṛga, due to a sin unknowingly committed by him (13. 69. 22; 13. 71. 2), had to live as a lizard in a deep well at Dvāravatī 13. 69. 1-4; Kṛṣṇa liberated him when the Yādavas were settling down at Dvāravatī 13. 71. 2-3; 13. 69. 25-29; (3) Śiva, in the form of Durvāsas, lived for a long time with Kṛṣṇa in his residence at Dvāravatī 13. 145. 35; (4) Yudhiṣṭhira asked Bhīṣ-ma the kind of gifts which one should give under different नक्षत्रस् (नक्षत्र-योगस्येदानीं दानकल्पं ब्रवीहि मे); Bhīṣma then told him what formerly Nārada, who had arrived at Dvārakā, told Devaki in reply to her question 13. 63. 1-4. F. Dvārakā as a holy place: Described as holy (पुण्या) 3. 86. 21; Yudhiṣṭhira, while on a pilgrimage, visited Dvārakā (यच् चापि तीर्थानि चरन्न् अगच्छं द्वारकां प्रति) 7. 85. 63; a holy place Piṇḍāraka located in Dvāravatī 3. 80. 82. G. Similes: (1) The city Dvārakā was well protected and well camouflaged and was furnished with all kinds of weapons as is done for the residence of Indra (सुरक्षितं सुगुप्-तं च सर्वायुधसमन्वितम् । तत् पुरं भरतश्रेष्ठ यथेन्द्रभवनं तथा ॥ ) 3. 16. 18; (2) As Indra left for heaven after killing his enemies so did Kṛṣṇa leave for Ānartapurī (when all the Kauravas were killed) 14. 51. 56; (3) Dvārakā, bereft of Vṛṣṇi heroes, compared with a woman who had lost her husband (द्वार-कां … मृतनाथां इव स्त्रियम्) 16. 6. 4; (4) In a long drawn metaphor Dvārakā compared to a river: the Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas were its water, horses its fishes, chariots its boats, the sound of musical instruments and the one produced by chariots its current, residences and holy bathing places its big crocodiles, jewels its thick layer of moss, ramparts made of वज्र its garlands, streets its whirlpools, cross-roads its steady, deep pieces of water, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa its big sharks; this river in the form of Dvārakā looked like the terrible Vaitaraṇī river having the noose of Kāla as its shark (ताम् स वृष्ण्यन्-धकजलां हयमीनां रथोडुपाम् । वादित्ररथघोषौघां वेश्मतीर्थमहा-ग्रहाम् ॥ रत्नशैवलसंघाटां वज्रप्रा-कारमालिनीम् । रथ्यास्रोतोजलावर्तां चत्व-रस्तिमितह्रदाम् ॥ रामकृष्णमहाग्राहां द्वारकासरितम् तदा । कालपाशग्रहां घो-रां नदीं वैतरणीम् इव ॥ ) 16. 6. 8-10; (5) Arjuna saw Dvārakā bereft of Vṛṣṇi heroes like a lotus pond in winter which is without its glory and gives no delight (गतश्रियं निरानन्दां पद्मिनीं शिशिरे यथा) 16. 6. 11.
द्वारपाल: Dvārapāla nt.: Name of a city (पुर) ? Nakula subjugated the city in his expedition to the west (प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2) before the Rājasūya (तथा वृन्दाटकं पुरम् । द्वारपालं च तरसा वशे चक्रे महाद्युतिः) 2. 29. 10.
दक्षिणमल्ल: Dakṣiṇamalla m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: In the east: Bhīma encountered them in his expedition to the east of Indraprastha before the Rājasūya (2. 23. 9; 2. 26. 1, 7); the southern Mallas are distinguished from the northern and the most northern Mallas (सोत्तमान् अपि चोत्तरान् मल्लानाम् अधिपम्) 2. 27. 3. B. Epic event: Bhīma, in his expedition to the east, expeditiously defeated them without having to use much force (ततो दक्षिणमल्लांश् च … तरसैवाजयद् भी मो नातितीव्रेण कर्मणा) 2. 27. 11 [See Malla, Mallarāṣṭra; and Uttamamalla and Uttara-malla in Addenda].
दक्षिनापथ: Dakṣināpatha m. (pl.): Name of the southern region; its people referred to as दक्षिणापथवासिन् (5. 19. 23). A. Characteristics: The people of Dakṣiṇāpatha are described as very heroic (महावीर्य) 5. 19. 23; Talavaras, Andhra-kas and others born in Dakṣiṇāpatha (दक्षिणापथजन्मानः) did not believe in Dhātṛ or Bhūtapati as being the अध्यक्ष of all the beings (12. 200. 33, 38); they are sinful; they roam over the earth; they lead the life of dogs, crows, बलस् (?), and vultures; they did not exist in the Kṛta age but are to be met with since the Tretāyuga 12. 200. 39-42 (for citation see Andhraka). B. Epic event: King Nīla of Māhiṣmatī, along with the heroic warriors of Dakṣiṇāpatha, joined the army of Duryodhana (दक्षिणापथवासिभिः) 5. 19. 23. C. Past event: Nala showed to Damayanti many paths which led to Dakṣiṇāpatha (एते गच्छन्ति बहवः पन्-थानो दक्षिणापथम्) 3. 58. 20 [See Dākṣiṇātya].
दरद: Darada m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: North: Arjuna defeated them along with Kāmbojas in his conquest of the north (2. 23. 9; 2. 24. 1) 2. 24. 22; listed by Saṃjaya among the northern म्लेच्छ peoples (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … शूद्राभीराथ दरदाः) 6. 10. 63, 66; also see E. Epic Events No. 3. below. B. Origin: They arose from the foam of the cow of Vasiṣṭha (तथैव दरदान् म्ले-च्छान् फेनतः सा ससर्ज ह) 1. 165. 36; Daradas mentioned among those Kṣatriyas who became वृषलस् due to not respect-ing Brāhmaṇas 13. 35. 17-18. C. Characte-risation: म्लेच्छस् 1. 165. 36; 6. 10. 63, 66; 7. 95. 13. D. Description: (1) Having faces like those of goats (बस्तमुख) 7. 97. 39; holding iron weapons and spears in hands (अयोहस्त, शूलहस्त) 7. 97. 39; very difficult to be conquered (सुदुर्जय) 7. 10. 17. E. Epic events: (1) Arjuna defeated them in his expedition before the Rājasūya 2. 24. 22; (2) Mentioned among those Kṣatriyas (क्षत्रियाः 2. 48. 16; राजन्याः 2. 48. 13) who brought riches by hundreds as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya (आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो जातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 12, 16; they were among those who acted as servers at the Rājasūya (यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 20, 22; (3) Pāṇḍavas had to cross their country before they could reach Subāhu's realm from Badarī 3. 174. 12; (4) Dru-pada suggested to Pāṇḍavas to send messen-gers to the kings of Daradas to seek their help in war 5. 4. 15; (5) On the second day of war, Daradas (on the side of the Pāṇḍavas) stood at the right side of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (दरदाश् चैव  … दुक्षिणं पक्षम् आश्रिताः) 6. 46. 49-50; (6) On the same day, Duryodhana with Daradas (on the side of the Kauravas) and others protected the army of Śakuni (दरदैश् … अभ्यरक्षत सौबलेयस्य वाहिनीम्) 6. 47. 16; (7) On the tenth day, Daradas, instigated by Duryodhana, attacked Arjuna to protect Bhīṣma 6. 112. 109; (8) On the twelfth day, Daradas were posted at the neck of the Suparṇa-vyūha (7. 19. 4) of Kauravas 7. 19. 8; (9) On the fourteenth day, Daradas were among those who were killed in large numbers by Arjuna 7. 68. 42-43; (10) On the same day, Sātyaki asked his charioteer to take him where Daradas, fighting with varied weapons (विविधायुधपाणयः) were posted to face him 7. 95. 13; Sātyaki repulsed with his नाराच arrows the stones hurled at him (अश्मवृष्टिम्) repeatedly by Daradas 7. 97. 35; (11) On the seventeenth day, Daradas were among those who survived to fight for Duryodhana; according to Kṛṣṇa they could not be conquered by any one except Arjuna (न शक्या युधी निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परंतप) 8. 51. 18, 20; (12) Kṛṣṇa had once defeated Daradas (दरदांश् च … जितवान् पुण्डरी-काक्षो … ) 7. 10. 17-18.
दर्व: Darva m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 37, 5; (दर्वीकाः सकचा दर्वा … ) 6. 10. 53 (is सकचाः name of a Janapada or description of Darvīkas and Darvas ?); mentioned among those Kṣatriyas who were degraded to the status of वृषल due to their not res-pecting Brāhmaṇas (वृषलत्वम् अनुप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 35. 17-18. [See Darvīka and Dārva].
दर्वीक: Darvīka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 37, 5; (दर्वीकाः सकचा दर्वा … ) 6. 10. 53 (for सकचाः see above Darva).
दर्शक: Darśaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 37, 5; (गान्धारा दर्श-कास् तथा) 6. 10. 52.
दशमालिक: Daśamālika m. (pl.): Name of one of the म्लेच्छ tribes. Listed by Saṃjaya among the nor-thern म्लेच्छस् of Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 5; (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना भरत-सत्तम) 6. 10. 63; (तथैव दशमालिकाः) 6. 10. 65; described as fierce (दारुणा म्लेच्छजातयः) 6. 10. 64.
दशापार्श्व: Daśāpārśva m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 37, 5; (वानायवो दशा-पार्श्वा … ) 6. 10. 54.
दशार्ण: Daśārṇa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people; the people or warriors of Daśārṇa also referred to as Dāśārṇa or Dāśārṇaka (f. -ikā). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; उत्तमौजा दशार्णाश् च 6. 10. 39; mention-ed as Janapada also in 4. 1. 9; were there two Daśārṇas: (1) one to the east of Hāstinapura, and (2) another to its south ?: (1) Bhīmasena in his conquest of the east (2. 26. 1, 7) reached Daśārṇa country after crossing Gaṇḍakī river and conquering the Videhas (ततः स गण्ड-कीं शूरो विदेहांश् च … । विजित्य … दशा-र्णान् अगमत् प्रभुः) 2. 26. 4; the name of their king was Sudharman (तत्र दाशार्णको राजा सुधर्मा) 2. 26. 5; (2) Daśārṇa also mentioned as surrounding the Kurus (परितः कुरून्) 4. 1. 9; before reaching the Matsya country Pāṇḍavas had to go along the north of Daśārṇa and the south of Pāñcāla (उत्तरेण दशार्णांस् ते पाञ्चालान् दक्षिणेन तु) 4. 5, 3; the name of their king was Hiraṇya-varman (स राजा दशार्णेषु … हिरण्य-वर्मा) 5. 190. 11. B. Description: Pleasing (रम्य) and rich in harvest (बह्वन्न) 4. 1. 9; sinful (आगस्कृत्) 1. 105. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 113. 25: आगस्कृतः चोरप्रायाः पर्वताद्याश्रयित्वात्); skilled in fighting while riding elephants (गज-योधिनः, गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 2-3; their name contains the word दश (?) (दशेरका दश दाशा दशार्णाः) 3. 134. 16. C. Epic events: (1) Pāṇḍu in his expedition after his marriage with Kuntī conquered first the Daśārṇas 1. 105. 8; (2) Kṛṣṇa told Karṇa that if he were to join Pāṇḍavas, Dāśārṇas would form part of his retinue (परिवारास् ते दाशार्णाश् च) 5. 138. 23; (3) On the second day of war, Dāśārṇakas (on the side of Pāṇḍavas) were stationed at the neck (दाशार्णकाः … ग्रीवायाम्) of the Krauñcā-ruṇavyūha of Pāṇḍavas 6. 46. 33, 46; (4) On that day the Daśārṇas (on the side of the Kauravas), led by Droṇa, followed Bhīṣma who was at the head of their Mahāvyūha 6. 47. 10, 12; (5) On the sixteenth day, instigated by Duryodhana, Daśārṇas riding elephants attacked Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna 8. 17. 3; (6) The Aśvamedha horse visited the Daśārṇas 14. 84. 5. D. Past event: Damayantī born in the Daśārṇa country (त्वं तु जाता … दशा-र्णेषु) 3. 66. 13. E. Different person(s) referred to variously: (i) King of Daśārṇas: दशार्ण Hiraṇyavarman 6. 91. 44; दशार्णराज Hiraṇyavarman 5. 190. 21; (also called Kāñcanavarman 5. 190. 20); 5. 193. 26; राजा दशार्णानाम् 7. 25. 28; राजा दशार्णेषु 5. 190. 11; दशार्णपति Hiraṇyavarman 5. 192. 8; 5. 193. 20; दशार्णाधिपति (1) Hiraṇyavarman 5. 190. 8, 16; 5. 192. 3; 5. 193. 11, 13; 6. 91. 23, 39, 42; 7. 25. 30; (2) Sudāman 3. 66. 12; दाशार्ण Hemavarman 5. 192. 12; 5. 193. 6; दाशार्णक (1) Hiraṇyavarman 5. 190. 9, 10, 19; (2) Sudharman 2. 26. 5; दाशार्णनृप Hiraṇyavarman 5. 193. 15; (ii) Messenger of Daśārṇa country: दूतं दाशार्णम् 5. 191. 11; (iii) Nurses of Daśārṇa country: धात्र्यो दाशार्णिकास् … 5. 190. 15.
दशार्ह: Daśārha, Dāśārha m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people. A. Description: Strong and large in number (बलवन्तश् च दाशार्हा बहवश् च) 1. 197. 25. B. Characteristic: Dāśā-rhas did not try to save their life in war (न हि … दाशार्हा रणे रक्षन्ति जीवितम्); they did not go the way the cowards and the unrighteous do, i. e. they did not avoid war; during the war they remained steadfast and did not run away from the battlefield (अयुद्धम् अनवस्थानं सं-ग्रामे च पलायनम् । भीरूणाम् असतां मार्गो नैष दाशार्हसेवितः ॥ 7. 85. 95-96; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 110. 98: अनवस्थानम् अस्थैर्यम्). C. Epic events: (1) Vidura told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that if Kṛṣṇa sided with Pāṇḍavas, the Dāśārha people (दाशार्हाः) would join him 1. 197. 25; (2) Nārada took leave of Yudhiṣṭhira to go to the town of the Dāśārha people (दाशार्ह-नगरीं प्रति) 2. 11. 71; (3) When Pra-dyumna was about to put his excellent arrow to the bow for discharging it against Śālva, all the Dāśārha warriors honoured it with blessings (तम् अर्चितं सर्वदा-शार्हपूगैः आशीर्भिर् … शरं ज्याम् अभि-नीयमानम्) 3. 20. 20; (4) When the Dāśārha people (दशार्हाः) saw the condi-tion of the Pāṇḍavas in forest, they shed tears due to grief 3. 118. 23; (5) Sātyaki desired the army of Daśārha warriors (दशार्हसेना) to attack Kaura-vas 3. 120. 5; but Yudhiṣṭhira desired the Daśārha heroes (दशार्हवीराः) to return to their country (and not march against Kauravas) 3. 120. 28; (6) Kṛṣṇa assured Yudhiṣṭhira that the Daśārha fighters would carry out the latter's orders (दशा-र्हयोधाः … निदेशं तव पालयन्ति) 3. 180. 21; he suggested that Hāstinapura with Dāśārha army consisting of horse-riders and foot-soldiers might wait for his return to Hāstinapura (दाशार्हयोधैस् तु ससादि-योधं प्रतीक्षताम् नागपुरं भवन्-तम्) 3. 180. 34; (7) Arjuna brought with him to Upaplavya the Dāśārha people from Ānarta (आनर्तेभ्यो ऽपि दाशार्हान्) 4. 67. 15; (8) Arjuna returned to Yudhiṣṭhira along with Kṛṣṇa and excellent Dāśārha persons (दाशार्हप्रवरैः) 5. 7. 36; (9) Bhīṣma and Droṇa wanted Duryodhana to make peace with Pāṇḍavas so that all kings headed by Dāśārha (= Kṛṣṇa ?) might shed tears of joy (दाशार्हप्रमुखा नृपाः) 5. 136. 17; (10) If Karṇa were to join the Pāṇḍavas, Dāśārha people would form part of his retinue (दाशार्हाः परिवारास् ते) 5. 138. 23; (11) The people of Daśārha country (दाशार्हाः) were angry when they saw Durvāsas yoking Rukmiṇī to a chariot and driving it in the city 13. 144. 27. D. Kṛṣṇa variously called as one belonging to the Daśārha country, the delighter, or protector, or king etc. of Daśārha people: (1) दशार्हनाथ 8. 12. 67; (2) दशार्हभर्ता 3. 180. 23; (3) दशार्हसिंह 3. 180. 22; (4) दशार्हाधि-पति 3. 24. 1; (5) दाशार्ह 3. 23. 46; 5. 90. 25; 5. 136. 17 (?); 8. 22. 47, 54; 8. 42. 57; (6) दाशार्हकुलनन्दन 12. 52. 9; दाशार्ह-नन्दन 1. 214. 26; (7) सर्वदाशार्ह-मुख्य 8. 45. 67. E. Princesses of the Daśārha country: दाशार्ही: (1) Jayā 1. 90. 35 (2) Śubhāṅgī 1. 90. 41; (3) Sudevā 1. 90. 38; (4) Śiśupāla's mother, (not named) 11. 25. 22; F. The Sabhā of the Daśārha people; दाशार्ही 2. 3. 24. [See Yādava, Vṛṣṇi].
दशेरक: Daśeraka, Dāśeraka m. (pl. sg.): Name of a country, and its people. A. Name explained: The name con-tains the word ‘ten’ (दश) (दशेरका दश दाशा दशार्णाः) 3. 134. 16. B. Epic events: (1) On the second day of war, hosts of Dāṣerakas stood at the ‘neck’ (ग्रीवायाम्) of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha 6. 46. 39 (Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (दाशेरकगणैः सह) 6. 46. 46; (2) On the third day, equipped (दंशिताः), they stood at the right wing (दक्षिणं पक्षम् आसाद्य) of the Garuḍavyūha (6. 52. 2) of Kauravas (दाशेरकगणैः सह) 6. 52. 8; (3) On the tenth day, instigated by Duryodhana, they attacked Arjuna to protect Bhīṣma (दाशेरकगणैः सह) 6. 112. 108; (4) On the twelfth day, Daśe-rakas (दशेरकाः) occupied the ‘neck’ of the Suparṇavyūha (7. 19. 8-9) of the Kauravas 7. 19. 7; (5) Dhṛtarāṣṭra men-tioned among Kṛṣṇa's exploits, his victory over Daśerakas (दशेरकान् … जितवान् पुण्ड-रीकाक्षः) 7. 10. 16, 18.
दस्यु: Dasyu m. (pl.): Designation of a class of people following a mode of life not approved by the law-makers; sometimes (especially in the Śāntiparvan) the term designates robbers; they moved in groups, hence sometimes referred to as दस्युगण। A. Location: Lived in the north-east (प्रागुत्तरां दिशं ये च वसन्त्य् आश्रित्य दस्यवः) 2. 24. 23; lived on mountains (दस्यून् पर्वतवासिनः) 2. 24. 15; lived in forests (अप्य् अरण्यं समाश्रित्य चरेद् दस्युगणैः सह) 12. 131. 10. B. Des-cription: Their heads shaven (लूनमूर्-धज) 7. 95. 40; sinful (पापकर्मन्), their minds obsessed by avarice (लोभोपहतचे-तस्), and their sight inauspicious (अशुभ-दर्शन) 16. 8. 45; cruel (क्रूर) 8. 49. 43; used sticks as weapons (यष्टिप्रह-रण) 16. 8. 47. C. Relations with other tribes: Ocassionally referred to as Śabara (तत्रावसत् … शबरालये) 12. 162. 34; (वासो मे शबरालये) 12. 162. 5; Yavanas, Kirātas, Gāndhāras, and many other tribes led the life of Dasyus (सर्वे ते दस्युजी-विनः) 12. 65. 13-15. D. Their degraded status in society revealed in many ways: (1) By comparing men who behaved improperly or unlawfully with Dasyus: (i) A poor man's begging is like an attack; he thereby annoys others like a Dasyu (याञ्चाम् आहुर् अनीशस्य अभिहारं च भारत । उद्वेजयति याचन् हि सदा भूतानि दस्युवत् ॥ ) 13. 59. 4 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 60. 4: अनीशस्य दरिद्रस्य । but अभिहारं तिरस्कारम्); (ii) A man of evil conduct considered mean like a Dasyu (दुराचारस् तु दुर्बुद्धिर् … दस्युर् इवा-धमः) 12. 166. 9; (iii) Ignorant men carry on their heads the burden of सं-सार by considering the wrong direction (as the right one) just as the Dasyus carry on their heads the load of flesh while following the wrong way (प्रकीर्ण-मेषभारो हि यद्वत् धार्येत दस्युभिः । प्रतिलोमां दिशं बुद्ध्वा संसारम् अबुधास् तथा ॥ ) 12. 208. 13 (Nī. Bom. Ed. 12. 215. 14 reads प्रकीर्णमेषभारं हि and explains: आमिषभारं वहन्तश् चोराः गम्यां दिशं राजकीयाद्यवरोधात् प्रति-कूलां बुध्वा (?) आमिषं त्यक्त्वान्यां दिशम् गच्छन्तो यथा न बध्यन्ते … प्रकीर्णमेषः विशस्तमेषः आमिषम् इत्य् अर्थः क्लीबत्वम् आर्षम् see Editors note on Vol. 16. p. 2169 where Arjunamiśra's reading मोष, meaning लोप्त्र ‘stolen pro-perty’, in place of मेष is preferred); but just as one should abandon the company of the Dasyus going the wrong way and follow the wholesome way, similarly one should give up doing actions dominated by रजस् and तमस् and gain happiness (तान् एव च यथा दस्यून् क्षिप्त्वा गच्छेच् छिवां दिशम् । तथा रजस्तमःकर्माण्य् उत्सृज्य प्राप्नुयात् सुखम्) 12. 208. 14; (iv) According to Maitreya what happened in the सभा of the Kauravas was like imi-tating the behaviour of Dasyus (दस्यूनाम् इव यद् वृत्तं सभायाम्) 3. 11. 17; (v) Draupadī told Virāṭa that his following the धर्म of Dasyus (since he did nothing to check Kīcaka) brought no credit to his Sabhā (दस्यूनाम् इव धर्मस् ते न हि संसदि शोभते) 4. 15. 24; (vi) Sātyaki's killing Bhūriśravas in the unlawful way was choosing the धर्म of Dasyus 7. 131. 2; (2) By referr-ing to the unlawful and dangerous acts of Dasyus: (i) Yavanas, Kirātas and others, though they lived in towns, followed the way of Dasyus (सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः) 12. 65. 15; (ii) Māndhātṛ told Indra that there were Dasyus living in disguise among all Varṇas and all the Āśramas (दृश्यन्ते मानवा लोके सर्ववर्णेषु दस्यवः । लिङ्गान्तरे वर्तमाना आश्रमेषु चतुर्ष्व् अपि ॥ ) 12. 65. 23; (iii) Yudhiṣṭhira asked Bhīṣma how should a Brāhmaṇa, who did not want to give up his sons and grandsons, live when the धर्म was at its lowest ebb, when all means of sub-sistence were under the control of Dasyus (सर्वस्मिन् दस्युसाद्भूते पृथिव्याम् उप-जीवने) 12. 130. 1 (दस्यु is equated with असाधु in 12. 130. 2-3); 12. 138. 1; 12. 139. 6; (iv) Dasyus have been killing men since old times thinking ‘they have wealth’; they torture men inflicting on them various punishments and always distress them (धनम् अस्येति पुरुषं पुरा निघ्नन्ति दस्यवः) 12. 171. 36; (v) As good men do not take what belongs to others, so do Dasyus not practise non-violence; people are pleased with Dasyus if they observe restraint (यथा सद्भिः परादानम् अहिंसा दस्युभिस् तथा । अनुरज्यन्ति भूतानि समर्यादेषु दस्युषु ॥ 12. 131. 14 (Nī., however, who reads दस्युभिः कृता on 12. 133. 15: सद्भिर् दस्युभिः परादानं परस्वहरणम् अपि कृतम् अहिंसा भवति तथा वक्ष्ये इति शेषः); (vi) Killing some one when he is not fighting, violation of wives of others, ungratefulness, robbing a Brāhmaṇa of his wealth, leaving him without any posse-ssions (निःशेषकरणं तथा), robbing women, coersion (परिस्थानम् cf. Critical Notes Vol. 14. p. 932), all this is practised by Dasyus and is censurable; and even if a Dasyu does not practise such acts, he is all the same a Dasyu (दस्युष्व् एतद् विगर्हितम् ॥ स एष एव भवति दस्युऋ एतानि वर्जयन्) 12. 131. 15-16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 133. 16: निःशेषकरणम् सर्वहरणम्); (vii) Death at the hands of a Dasyu is considered wretched (प्राकृतो वध उच्यते) and is equated with death due to poison, hanging, or burns, or due to getting killed by animals having jaws 12. 286. 25 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 297. 25 seems to explain प्राकृत as दुर्म-रण cf. योगी अत्यन्तव्याधिपीडाग्रस्तो ऽपि दुर्मरणं नेच्छेद् इत्य् अर्थः); (viii) Dasyus are the limit; (1) even Dasyus do not trust in those who act merci-lessly (दस्यवो ऽप्य् उपशङ्कन्ते निरनु-क्रोशकारिणः) 12. 131. 11; (2) even Dasyus trust ascetics (तापसेषु हि विश्वा-सम् अपि कुर्वन्ति दस्यवः) 12. 87. 28; (3) The Rākṣasas refused to eat the flesh of the mean Gautama, and suggested that it might be distributed among the Dasyus; but even Dasyus did not wish to eat the flesh of the sinful and unfaithful Gautama, nor the beasts of prey 12. 166. 18-19, 22-23; (ix) Dasyus are equated with impious men; when Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura were born, there were no Dasyus in the Kuru land, nor other impious men (नाभवन् दस्यवः केचिन् नाधर्मरुचयो जनाः) 1. 102. 5; (x) If Brāhmaṇas parted company with Kṣatri-yas, the latter became degraded and were as good as Dasyus (अपध्वस्ता दस्यु-भूता भवन्ति ये ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियान् संत्यजन्ति) 12. 74. 10. E. The Duties of Dasyus: On being questioned by Māndhātṛ about the धर्म of Dasyus (कथं धर्मं चरेयुस् ते 12. 65. 15), Indra told him in details the duties of Dasyus which included service (शुष्रूषा) to parents, teachers, elders, ascetics and kings, gifts to twice-born, observance of non-violence, truth, purity, faithfulness and other virtues 12. 65. 17-22; a Dasyu who lived within limits did not perish after his death; this is illustrated by the narrative of Kāpavya; those Dasyus who observed their धर्म achieved perfections (अपि ते दस्यवो भूत्वा क्षि-प्रं सिद्धिम् अवाप्नुयुः) 12. 133. 1-22. F. Limitations of Dasyus: They are not able to overpower a person who has no desires and one who is free from (the fear of) loss of wealth (न च दस्यवः । प्रभवन्ति धनज्यानिनिर्मुक्तस्य निरा-शिषः) 12. 170. 12. G. King's relationship with Dasyus: Indra created for a king his duty and armour, weapon and bow, for killing Dasyus (इन्द्रेणेदं दस्युवधाय कर्म उत्पादितं वर्म शस्त्रं धनुश् च) 5. 29. 27 (But Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 29. 30: कर्म युद्धं); Brahman created Kṣatriyas for killing Dasyus who obstruct-ed those that were engaged in agriculture, cattle-care, trade, and also those who performed the duties of Hotṛ, Adhvaryu and Udgātṛ priests (ऊर्ध्वं चैव त्रयी विद्या) 12. 90. 7-8 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 89. 7: ऊर्ध्वं स्वर्गम्); a Kṣatriya should always be ready to kill Dasyus in battles 12. 60. 14; for a king, there is no higher duty than destroying Dasyus 12. 60. 17; their absence, (as also of beggars), in a kingdom considered desirable 12. 89. 20; a king should take his subjects into confidence by drawing their attention to the danger posed by his enemies who collaborated with Dasyus 12. 88. 26; a king must protect all the वर्णस् if the Dasyus tried to plunder their wives and possessions 13. 47. 44; a king who saved the beings from Dasyus and gave them wealth and happiness was a great king (दस्युभ्यः प्राणदानात् स धनदः सुखदो विराट्) 12. 98. 8; if a king did not protect his subjects, they could be at the mercy of Dasyus (लोको ऽयं दस्युसाद् भवेत्) 12. 68. 20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 68. 20: दस्युसात् चोराधी-नाः); if due to a king's negligence his subjects were being robbed, such a king was Kali 12. 12. 27; Yudhiṣṭhira wanted to know if there were boundaries beyond which he should not allow Dasyus to step (अस्ति स्विद् दस्युमर्यादा याम् अहं परिवर्जये) 12. 140. 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 142. 1: दस्यूनाम् अकार्यकारिणाम् अपि मर्यादा काचिद् अस्ति इतो ऽधिकं दस्यूनां न कर्तव्यम् इति); when a king behaved dis-regarding all restraints and in such a state Dasyus brought about total confusion, then if all वर्णस् took up weapons (to protect themselves) no blemish attached to them (उन्मर्यादे प्रवृत्ते तु दस्युभिः संकरे कृते । सर्वे वर्णा न दुष्येयुः शस्त्र-वन्तो … ) 12. 79. 18; if the power of Dasyus increased (अभ्युत्थिते दस्युबले), then even a Brāhmaṇa, Vaiśya or Śūdra should hold the rod of punishment in hand and protect the subjects from Dasyus; any one, Śūdra or some one else, whom the subjects, when tortured by Dasyus, turned for protection should be honoured (12. 79. 34-35, 38); a king in whose dominion hordes of Dasyus freely plundered the posse-ssions of others, as do crows the fishes in water, was contemptible among the Kṣatriyas (स वै क्षत्रियपांसनः) 12. 140. 28; Dasyus overpower a kingdom which has no ruler and which is weak (अनि-न्द्रम् अबलं राष्ट्रं दस्यवो ऽभिभवन्ति च) 12. 67. 2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 67. 2: अनिन्द्रं अराजकं अत एवाबलम्); kings in whose dominion Brāhmaṇas were with-out proper means of subsistence, their oxen and draught-animals did not prosper, the churning pot (i. e. the curds in it) was not churned (because the pot was empty) when it was gifted, they became degraded like Dasyus (नैषाम् उक्षा वर्धते नोत वाहा न गर्गरो मथ्यते संप्रदाने । अप-ध्वस्ता दस्युभूता भवन्ति येषां राष्ट्रे ब्राह्मणा वृत्तिहीनाः) 12. 329. 12 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 342. 19: गर्गरः दधी-क्षुतैलादिनिपीडनयन्त्रम् । येषां राज्ञां कृष्यादिहीनत्वात् तादृशा राजानो नष्टाश् चोराश् च भवन्तीत्य् अर्थः; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 68. 23: गर्गरा मन्थन्यः on the authority of Medinī); if a king and his Brāhmaṇa Purohita were opposed to each other, Dasyus took the side of him who was stronger of the two (अन्वग्बलं दस्यवस् तद् भजन्ते) 12. 74. 8 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 73. 7: अनु पश्चात् प्रकाशमा-नं बलम् अन्वग्बलं यथा स्यात् तथा); a king might take away the wealth of Dasyus (and of those who did not perform sacri-fices) 12. 134. 2; a king should always kill Dasyus and should not pardon any one on any account (निहन्यात् सर्वतो दस्यून् न कामात् कस्यचित् क्षमेत्) 12. 76. 5; Dyumatsena told Satyavant that if Dasyus were not awarded capital punish-ment, there would be chaos everywhere; in the Kali age, one would say: ‘this was mine, not his’ and normal life would be impossible (लोकयात्रा न चैव स्यात्) 12. 259. 6 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 267. 6: लोकयात्रा तीर्थगमनवाणिज्या-दिव्यवहारः कलौ युगे अधर्मप्र-धाने काले); however, a king should be careful while giving capital punishment to Dasyus, because when a Dasyu died, many other innocents dependent on him, like his wife, mother, father, son, also got killed for no fault of theirs (राजा तस्माट् सम्यक् प्रधारयेत्) 12. 259. 10; but, a Dasyu, in fact, did not belong to men, nor to gods, nor to Gandharvas, nor to Pitṛs; for no one belonged to any one (कः कस्येह न कश्चन) 12. 259. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 267. 21: दस्युवधे तद्-भार्यादीनां वधो नास्तीत्य् अर्थः । सम्-बन्धाभावात्); entering into an agreement (with Dasyus) who were ignorant and of confused mind was like trying to find a lotus in a cemetery or godliness in a Piśāca (i. e. trying to do what was impossible) (पद्मं श्मशानाद् आदत्ते पिशाचाच् चापि दैवतम् । तेषु यः समयं कुर्याद् अज्ञेषु हतबुद्धिषु ॥ ) 12. 259. 22 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 267. 22: पद्मं शवालङ्-कार(? °रम्) आदत्ते पिशाचात् पिशाचोपह-तात् । आदत्ते चैलादिकम् इति शेषः॑कीदृशं समयं दैवतं देवताशपथादिरूपम् । ; also cf. Critical Notes to Vol. 16 (p. 2193) on 12. 259. 22: “Lotus does not grow in cemetery, and if it does, it is not consi-dered as holy. Similarly one does not expect good conduct or divine grace from persons possessed by ghosts. Cp. (i. e. the commentary of Paramānanda Bhaṭṭācārya) remarks at the end as follows: तद् यथा पद्मं स्वगुणैर् उत्कृष्टं श्मशानाद् उपादाय कश्चिच् छिरसि कुर्याद् देवाय वा दद्यात्, तत्राश्वसीत कः । भाविपिशाचाद्यु पद्रवाशङ्किचेताः स्यात्-इत्य् अर्थः); a king who, following the Śāstra, teaches Dasyus to pay attention to place and time is not touched by sin (देशकालप्रतीक्षे यो दस्योर् दर्शयते नृपः । शास्त्रजां बुद्धिम् आस्थाय नैनसा स हि युज्यते ॥ ) 12. 25. 11 (Nī., however, who reads मर्षयते in Bom. Ed. 12. 24. 11: मर्षयते दस्यून् अपि न हन्ति एनसा तज्जेन पापेन); in bad times, if a king had to take resort to a forest and live with Dasyus he should not associate with Dasyus who threw all norms of behaviour to the winds; it was easy to raise an army of Dasyus (of good behaviour) for performing fear-ful acts (अप्य् अरण्यं समाश्रित्य चरेद् दस्युगणैः सह । न त्व् एवोद्धृतमर्या-दैर् दस्युभिः सहितश् चरेत् । दस्यूनां सुलभा सेना रौद्रकर्मसु भारत) 12. 131. 10 (but Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 133. 11: दस्युभिः दस्युप्रायैर् अमात्यैः); when a king considered himself more prosperous than his (Dasyu) adversaries, he should turn on them and strike the (horde of) Dasyus without hesitation (यदा बहु-विधां वृद्धिम् मन्यते प्रतिलोमतः । तदा विवृत्य प्रहरेद् दस्यूनाम् अविचार-यन् ॥ ) 12. 104. 38 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 103. 39: प्रतिलोमतः शत्रोर् अपेक्षया विवृत्य प्रकटीभूय दस्यूनां दस्यून्); Dasyus should not thoroughly annihilate even those who happened to be under their control; they should not act in a cruel manner thinking that they were very strong (तस्मात् सशेषं कर्तव्यं स्वाधीनम् अपि दस्युभिः । न बलस्थो ऽहम् अस्मीति नृशंसानि समाचरेत्) 12. 131. 17; Dasyus, if not forced to remain within certain limits of behaviour, acted as robbers (निर्मर्यादा दस्यवस् तु भवन्ति परि-पन्थिनः) 12. 101. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 100. 3: ये ऽर्थधर्मयोर् निर्मर्-यादास् ते परिपन्थीनो नाशका भवन्ति). H. Epic events: (1) Arjuna, in his conquest of the north before the Rāja-sūya, conquered Dasyus who lived on mountains (दस्यून् पर्वतवासिनः) 2. 24. 15; he also conquered the Dasyus living in the forest in the northeast (प्रागुत्तरां दिशम् ये च वसन्त्य् आश्रित्य दस्यवः । निवसन्ति वने ये च) 2. 24. 23; (2) Yudhiṣṭhira asked Saṃjaya whether the Kauravas, if they encountered the bands of Dasyus, remembered Arjuna 5. 23. 19; (3) Arjuna told Saṃjaya that when he would scatter the hordes of Dasyus gather-ed for the battle, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and his sons would repent 5. 47. 59; (4) On the fourteenth day of war, Sātyaki covered the earth with the shaven heads of Dasyus together with their headgears 7. 95. 40; he killed many Dasyus 7. 97. 20; (5) Kṛṣṇa told Babhru to protect the Yādava women so that they were not attacked by Dasyus due to their greed for wealth (नैता हिं-स्युर् दस्यवो वित्तलोभात्) 16. 5. 4; (6) When Arjuna stopped at Pañcanada on his way to Hāstinapura with Vṛṣṇi women, Dasyus became greedy and took counsel among themselves; then, thousands of them, using sticks as weapons, attacked Vṛṣṇis desirous of looting property; they disregarded Arjuna's warning and continued their attack; Arjuna could not check them as he forgot his अस्त्रस्; the Vṛṣṇi warriors could not stop Dasyus running away with Vṛṣṇi women; Arjuna and the Vṛṣṇi warriors killed some of the plundering Dasyus with arrows; when Arjuna's arrows were exhausted, he killed Dasyus with the tip of his bow; but that was of no avail; before his very eyes, Dasyus (म्लेच्छस्) took away Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka women 16. 8. 44-61. I. Past events: (1) Nahuṣa, during his rule, had killed hordes of Dasyus 1. 70. 26; (2) Yayāti pleased the Dasyus by completely controlling them (अतर्पयद् … दस्यून् संनिग्रहेण च) 1. 80. 3-4; (3) Dasyus who had stolen wealth, when pursued by royal guards, reached the hermitage of Māṇḍavya; they kept the loot in the आश्रम and hid themselves due to fear; the guards asked Māṇḍavya which way the Dasyus had fled; when Māṇḍavya did not reply they searched the आश्रम and found the hidden thieves (चोरान्); the guards reported them and Māṇḍavya to the king; the king asked to kill the thieves (Dasyus) and Māṇḍavya (तं राजा सह तैश् चोरैर् अन्वशाद् वध्यताम् इति) 1. 101. 4-11; (4) some Dasyus were in search of men who, afraid of the Dasyus, had entered a forest; the Dasyus asked the ascetic Kauśika which way the men had disappeared; Kauśika told them that they had taken resort to the forest; the cruel Dasyus found them out and killed them 8. 49. 43-45; (5) Aśvagrīva (= Hayagrīva), whose limbs were cut off while fighting with Dasyus, enjoyed life in heaven 12. 25. 25; (6) In order to illustrate that a Dasyu, who observed proper limits, did not perish after death (यथा दस्युः समर्यादः प्रेत्यभावे न नश्यति) is told the story of Kāpavya; he was born of a Niṣādī by a Kṣatriya; he obtained perfection on account of his being a (good) Dasyu (since he lived righteously carrying out the duties of a Kṣatriya) (दस्युत्वात् सिद्धिम् आप्तवान्); when the Brāhmaṇas, who had retired to a forest, did not accept food brought to them by Kāpavya because he was a Dasyu, he left some of it in their homes and went away early in the morning; many Dasyus who behaved cruelly disregarding the rules elected Kāpavya as their leader; they agreed to live as instructed by him and requested him to act as their father and mother; he taught them the way they should live and ended by saying that Dasyus, if they observed the rules of धर्म, would obtain perfection in spite of their being Dasyus (ये पुनर् धर्म-शास्त्रेण वर्तेरन्न् इह दस्यवः । अपि ते दस्यवो भूत्वा क्षिप्रं सिद्धिम् अवा-प्नुयुः ॥ ); the Dasyus carried out the instructions of Kāpavya and abstained from sinful deeds; Kāpavya, who by his act turned the Dasyus away from committing sins, obtained great perfection (मह तीं सिद्धिम् आप्तवान् । साधूनाम् आचरन् क्षेमं दस्यून् पापान् निवर्तयन् ॥ ) 12. 133. 1-24; (7) A certain Brāhmaṇa, Gautama by name, happened to take shelter in the house of a wealthy Dasyu who was truthful and generous; Gautama got from the Dasyu new garments and wife; he lived there happily and helped the Dasyu to maintain his family; like the Dasyus, Gautama began to kill geese (वक्राङ्गान्) with arrows (Nī. who reads चक्राङ्गान् explains it as हंसान्, Bom. Ed. 12. 168. 36): the Brāhmaṇa Gautama, due to contact with Dasyus and leading their life, became similar to them (दस्युभिः समताम् इयात्); many months passed while Gautama lived happily in the settlement of the Dasyus (दस्युग्रामे) killing many birds (पक्षिणः); once another Brāhmaṇa happened to arrive in that settlement of the Dasyus (दस्युग्रामम्); in that settlement which was full of Dasyus (ग्रामे दस्यु-जनाकीर्णे) he searched everywhere for a Brāhmaṇa; he entered the house where Gautama lived; he recognized that Gautama belonged to Madhyadeśa; he asked Gau-tama how he came to live like a Dasyu (मध्यदेशपरिज्ञातो दस्युभावं गतः कथम्) 12. 162. 29-44. J. Mytho-logical events: Gods appointed Kṛṣṇa to kill Dasyus (here Asura Naraka and his Asura followers are meant by the word Dasyu) (न्ययोजयन् दस्युवधाय कृष्णम्) 5. 47. 74, 76. K. Future event: Kalki will always be engaged in killing Dasyus; they would perish crying pitiable words like ‘oh father, oh son’ (कल्किश् चरिष्यति महीं सदा दस्यु-वधे रतः ॥ हा तात हा सुतेत्य् एवं तास् ता वाचः सुदारुणाः । विक्रोशमानान् सुभृशं दस्यून् नेष्यति संशयम् ॥ ) 3. 189. 5-6.
दाक्षिणात्य: Dākṣiṇātya m. (pl.): Designation of the people or warriors of the south; certain kings of the south designated as दाक्षिणात्य। A. Description: Brave (शूर) 5. 30. 24; excellent warriors (प्रवीर) 8. 17. 2; cruel and rough in battles (क्रूर, सं-ग्रामकर्कश) 8. 15. 10; fighting with swords and shields (असिचर्मिन्) 12. 102. 5; also expert in fighting with all kinds of weapons and missiles (सर्वशस्त्रास्त्र-कुशल) 6. 16. 17; also fought from chariots and riding elephants (दाक्षिणात्या … रथाः 5. 196. 6; गजयोधिन् 8. 17. 2). B. Status: According to the Rākṣasa Kal-māṣapāda, the Dākṣiṇātyas were degraded persons (वृषला दाक्षिणात्याः) 8. 30. 73. C. Epic events: (1) A certain king of the south brought for Yudhiṣṭhira an armour at the time of the Rājasūya (दाक्षिणात्यः संनहनम्) 2. 49. 7; (2) Kings of the south sided with Duryodhana to fight with Pāṇḍavas (दाक्षिणात्याः … राजानः) 5. 30. 23-24; (3) Ulūka men-tioned Dākṣiṇātyas among those who sided with Duryodhana 5. 158. 20; (4) Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that killing Dākṣiṇātya warriors would be Bhīmasena's responsi-bility (दाक्षिणात्याश् च भीमसेनस्य भा-गतः) 5. 56. 14; (5.) Chariot-fighters from the south along with others started to-wards Kurukṣetra (दाक्षिणात्याः … ये रथाः) 5. 196. 6; (6) Duryodhana ex-pected the Dākṣiṇātya warriors to protect Bhīṣma in the war 6. 16. 17; (7) On the eighth day of war, Bhīṣma, with Dākṣiṇātya warriors, stood at the head of his Mahāvyūha (अग्रतः सर्वसैन्यानाम्  … दाक्षिणात्यैश् च) 6. 83. 5-6; (8) On the eleventh day, Dākṣiṇātyas and others took position at the extreme end (प्र-पक्ष) of the left wing (सव्यं पार्श्वम्) of the Śakaṭavyūha of the Kauravas (7. 6. 4, 7, 15); (9) On the fourteenth day, the large army of Dākṣiṇātyas stood immedia-tely behind the army of Āvantyas close to Droṇa; according to Sātyaki, the southern warriors were no match for Arjuna (उदीच्या दाक्षिणात्याश् च … एते ऽर्जुनस्य क्रुद्ध-स्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्) 7. 86. 28-29; Sātyaki asked his charioteer to drive his chariot towards Dākṣiṇātya warriors who were led by Karṇa (दाक्षिणात्यं महा-बलम्) 7. 88. 30, (दाक्षिणात्याश् च बहवः सूतपुत्रपुरोगमाः) 7. 88. 34; (10) On the sixteenth day, Kṛpa, along with the Dākṣiṇātya warriors stood at the right foot of Makaravyūha of the Kauravas (पादे तु दक्षिणे राजन्) 8. 7. 14, 18; on that day, Pāṇḍya had killed many Dākṣiṇātyas and others with his arrows after depriving them of their weapons and armours (विशस्त्र-कवचान् बाणैः कृत्वा) 8. 15. 10; (11) On the sixteenth day, Dākṣiṇātyas mentioned among those who, at the instance of Duryo-dhana, attacked Dhṛṣṭadyumna 8. 17. 1-2; (12) On the seventeenth day, Arjuna was proud that he had cut off Dākṣiṇātyas during the war (दाक्षिणात्या विशस्ताः) 8. 49. 96; (13) At the end of the seventeen days of war, Saṃjaya mentioned Dākṣiṇātyas among those who lost their lives while fighting 8. 4. 47; at the end of the eighteen days of war, all Dākṣiṇātyas were killed (हता … दाक्षिणात्याश् च सर्वशः) 9. 1. 27; (14) Among the past exploits of Kṛṣṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra mentioned Kṛṣṇa's victory over Dākṣiṇātyas (दाक्षिणात्यांश् च … जितवान् पुण्डरीकाक्षः) 7. 10. 16, 18; Vasudeva too remembered Kṛṣṇa's defeating Dākṣiṇātyas 16. 7. 11. D. Past event: King Vyuṣi-tāśva defeated, captured and carried off kings of the south (स विजित्य गृहीत्वा च नृपतीन् … दाक्षिणात्यान् अकालयत्) 1. 112. 11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 121. 12: अकालयत् वशीकृतवान्). E. Kings characterized generally as ‘southerner(s)’ or king of Dākṣiṇātyas: (1) दाक्षिणात्यः 2. 49. 7; (2) दाक्षिणात्यान् महीपान् 3. 119. 18; दाक्षिणात्याश् च … राजानः 3. 226. 3; (ये राजानः) 5. 30. 23-24; णृपाः 7. 68. 32; (3) Rukmī was the son of the king of Dākṣi-ṇātyas (viz. Bhīṣmaka) (दाक्षिणात्यपतेः पुत्रो … ) 5. 155. 2. [See Dakṣiṇāpatha].
दार्व: Dārva m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: In the north (or north-west (दिशं धनपतेर् … 2. 23. 1; प्रय-याव् उत्तरां … दिशम्) 2. 24. 1; (for location also see Epic events No. 3 below). B. Description: Fierce and doing cruel acts (उग्र, क्रूरकर्मन्) 8. 51. 18. C. Epic events: (1) Arjuna in his expedi-tion to the north before the Rājasūya defeated the Dārva Kṣatriyas along with Trigartas and Kokanadas 2. 24. 17; (2) The royal Kṣatriyas among Dārvas brought riches in hundreds as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya 2. 48. 12 (राजन्याः 2. 48. 13; क्षत्रियाः 2. 48. 16); (3) Starting from Badarī, Pāṇḍavas crossed the country of Dārvas on the difficult terrain of Himavant before they reached Subhāhu's realm (चीनांस् … सदार्वान्  … अतीत्य दुर्गं हिमवत्प्रदेशं पुरं सुबाहोर् ददृशुर् नृवीराः) 3. 174. 12; (4) On the fourteenth day of war, innu-merable Dārvas were killed by Arjuna 7. 68. 42-43; (5) On the seventeenth day, they were among those who had gathered round the Kuru warriors for the sake of Duryodhana; according to Kṛṣṇa they could not be conquered by any one except Arjuna (दार्वाभिसारा … एते सुयोधन-स्यार्थे शंरब्धाः कुरुभिः सह । न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परं-तप ॥ ) 8. 51. 18, 20.
दाश: Dāśa m. (pl.): Name of a people. According to Aṣṭāvakra, there are ten Dāśas (दशेरका दश दाशा दशार्णाः) 3. 134. 16.
दासमीय: Dāsamīya (Daśamīya) m. (pl.): Name of a settlement of degraded Brāh-maṇas (?). A. Location: North-west; They are mentioned along with Āraṭṭas and Vrātyas 8. 30. 36. B. Character: According to a Brāhmaṇa who visited the Kauravas, the Dāsamīya people were irreligious and hence one should not visit their country (आरट्टा नाम ते देशा नष्टधर्मान् न तान् व्रजेत् । व्रात्यानां दासमीयानाम्) 8. 30. 36; Karṇa told Śalya that the Dāśamīyas performed inauspicious deeds even in the Kṛta age (दाशमीयानाम् कृते ऽप्य् अशुभ-कर्मणाम्) 8. 30. 66 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 45. 20: कृते कृतयुगे ऽपि). C. Epic events: (1) They brought tribute of three billions of gold for the Rājasūya, but were not allowed to enter the gate; when they brought additional tribute in the form of shining golden कमण्डलुस् they were allow-ed to enter (दासमीयाश् च सर्वशः । … त्रिखर्वं बलिम् आदाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारि-ताह् ॥ कमण्डलून् उपादाय जातरूपमयाञ् शुभान् । एवं बलिं प्रदायाथ प्रवेशं लेभिरे ततः ॥ ) 2. 47. 5-6 (Nī., Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 5 reads दासनीयाः and explains दास्ययोग्याः शूद्रादयः ब्राह्मणा एव वा तादृशाः); (2) Their large armies, consisting of horse-fighters, charioteers, and elephant-riders which went to the battlefield, were killed by Arjuna (गोवा-सदासमीयानां … उदीर्णाश् च महासेना ब्रह्मक्षत्रस्य … ॥ त्वां समासाद्य निधनं गताः साश्वरथद्विपाः) 8. 51. 16-17.
दीप्ताक्ष: Dīptākṣa: Name of a people. Mentioned by Bhīma among the sixteen people whose kings extirpated their kinsmen and friends together with their relatives; their king's name was Purūravas (दीप्ताक्षा-णां पुरूरवाः) 5. 72. 15.
दीर्घवेणु: Dīrghaveṇu m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: They lived between the mountains Meru and Mandara, along the river Śailodā; they enjoyed the pleasing shade of bamboos and reeds (मेरु-मन्दरयोर् मध्ये शैलोदाम् अभितो नदीम् । ये ते कीचकवेणूनां छायां रम्याम् उपा-सते ॥ ) 2. 48. 2-3. B. Epic event: Their kings brought as tribute for the Rājasūya heaps of gold of the variety called पिपीलिक, given as boon by ants (?), to be measured by द्रोणस् (for citation see Ekāśanajyoha).
दुगूल: Dugūla m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the nor-thern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबो-ध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (दुगूलाः प्रतिमत्स्याश् च) 6. 10. 50.
दुन्दुभिस्वन: Dundubhisvana m. (sg.): Name of one of the Deśas of the Krauñcadvīpa. It is the last of the Deśas enumerated of the Krauñcadvīpa; it is situated beyond Munideśa (मुनिदेशात् परश् चैव प्रोच्यते दुन्दुभिस्वनः) 6. 13. 22; it is full of Siddhas and Cāraṇas and the people there in general are white in complexion; it is also frequented by gods and Gandharvas (सिद्धचारणसंकीर्णो गौरप्रायो जना-धिप । एते देशा महाराज देवगन्धर्व-सेविताः) 6. 13. 22-23.
दुर्वारण: Durvāraṇa m. (pl.): Name of a section of the Kāmbojas (?). A. Characteristics: They were chariot-fighters; their chariots bore golden banners (ये त्व् एते रथिनो राजन् दृश्यन्ते काञ्चन-ध्वजाः); they were brave (शूर), profi-cient in sciences (कृतविद्य), expert in archery (धनुर्वेदे च निष्ठिताः); keep-ing close to each other, they wished to work for the welfare of their comrades in wars (संहतास् च भृशं ह्य् एते अन्योन्यस्य हितैषिणः). B. Epic events: An अक्षौ-हिणी of them had gathered for Duryo-dhana; protected by the Kuru hero, they were waiting for Sātyaki's attack; watch-ful, they came close to Sātyaki; Sātyaki assured Yudhiṣṭhira that he would destroy them as does fire the grass 7. 87. 42-45; (दुर्वारण name of a people or an adje-ctive ‘difficult to resist’ of Kāmbojas ?).
दुर्विभाग: Durvibhāga m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their Kṣatriyas brought riches by hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (औदुम्बरा दुर्विभागाः … आहार्षुः क्ष-त्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 12, 16.
द्रमिड: Dramiḍa (Dramiḷa), Draviḍa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (द्रविडाः केरलाः प्राच्या … ) 6. 10. 57; Yudhiṣṭhira went to the south to reach the Draviḍa country (प्रययौ दक्षिणा-मुखः) 3. 117. 18; 3. 118. 4; Arjuna fought with the Draviḍas when he reached the southern ocean (प्रययौ … दक्षिणं सलिलार्णवम्) 14. 84. 10. B. Origin: (1) Created, along with the Puṇḍras and others, by Nandinī, the cow of Vasiṣṭha, from her foam (द्रमिडान् … फेनतः सा ससर्ज ह) 1. 165. 36; (2) They are listed among those Kṣatriyas who were degraded on account of not respecting Brāhmaṇas (द्रमिऌआश् च कलिङ्गाश् च … तास् ताः क्षत्रियजातयः । वृषलत्वं परि-गता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 33. 20-21; (द्रमिडाः) 13. 35. 17; they became degraded due to their neglect of the duties of a Kṣatriya (त एते द्रमिडाः … वृषल-त्वं परिगता व्युत्थानात् क्षत्रधर्मतः) 14. 29. 16. C. Description: of terrific valour (उग्रविक्रम) 8. 4. 46. D. Epic events: (1) Sahadeva, in his expedition to the south (2. 28. 1, 8, 37) subjugated the Draviḍas by just sending messengers to them and made them pay tribute for the Rājasūya (द्रविडांश् चैव … दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत्) 2. 28. 48; (2) Draviḍas mentioned among those whose kings attended the Rāja-sūya of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 31. 12; Kṛṣṇa saw them who, afraid of the luster of the arms, attended the Rājasūya and acted as servers (आगतान् अहम् अद्राक्षं यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 22; (3) In his pilgrimage Yudhiṣṭhira, going south along the river Godāvarī, reached the sea in the Draviḍa country before going to the Agastyatīrtha and the Nārītīrthas (द्रवि-डेषु … समुद्रम् आसाद्य) 3. 118. 4; (4) Kṛṣṇa told Karṇa that the Draviḍas would be among those who would lead his proce-ssion if he joined the Pāṇḍavas (पुरोगमाश् च ते सन्तु द्रविडाः सह कुन्तलैः) 5. 138. 25; (5) Ulūka mentioned Draviḍas among those who had joined the army of Duryodhana (राजचमूं समेताम् … द्रविडान्ध्रकाञ्च्यैः) 5. 158. 19-20; (6) On the sixteenth day of the war, Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna, along with the Draviḍas (on the side of the Pāṇḍavas), attacked the Kaurava army (द्रविडैः) 8. 8. 14; (7) On the seventeenth day, the Draviḍa foot-soldiers (on the side of Pāṇḍavas), in-cited by Sātyaki, attacked Karṇa; Karṇa cut off with his arrows their arms and head-gears and felled them down (द्रविड°  … अभ्यर्दयञ् … कर्णं आहवे ते विबाहु-शिरस्त्राणाः … प्रहताः कर्णसायकैः पेतुः पृथिव्यां) 8. 33. 4-5; (8) Saṃjaya listed Draviḍas among those who were killed in the first seventeen days of war (द्रविडाश् चोग्रविक्रमाः … निहताः) 8. 4. 46, 48; (9) Arjuna had to fight with the Draviḍas (द्रविडैर्) when he accompanied the Aśvamedha horse 14. 84. 11. E. A Dramiḍa king occurs in a comparison: The glorious Aśoka tree, according to Dama-yantī, with its chaplets (of blossoms), shone like the glorious king of Dramiḍas (अहो बतायम् अगमः श्रीमान् … आपीडैर् बहुभिर् भाति श्रीमान् द्रमिडराड् इव) 3. 61. 98 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 64. 103: अगमः वृक्षः आपीडैः पुष्पफलादिरूपैर् अलं-कारैः).
द्वैधेय: Dvaidheya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कुट्टापरान्ता द्वैधेयाः) 6. 10. 47.
द्व्यक्ष: Dvyakṣa m. (pl.): Name of a people. They brought ample gold and silver as tribute for the Rājasūya but were stopped at the gate (द्व्यक्षांस् … समा-गतान् … द्वारि वारितान् । बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्मै हिरण्यं रजतं बहु 2. 47. 15-16.
